cardiff.seoTitle: Schools in Cardiff Catchment 2026 - Postcode Map & List
cardiff.seoDescription: Cardiff area catchment finder: 124 schools, every catchment boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year - free.
paragraphs: Cardiff's 124 schools span every phase from nursery through to sixth form, making it the largest concentration of state schools in Wales. Admissions are coordinated by Cardiff Council, which publishes catchment boundaries and oversubscription criteria each September for the following academic year.

Because Cardiff is a bilingual city, many schools offer Welsh-medium education alongside English-medium provision - and catchment areas for Welsh-medium schools are typically wider to reflect lower pupil density. Check each school's admissions policy carefully, as Welsh-medium and English-medium catchments rarely overlap.

solihull.seoTitle: Solihull School Catchment Map 2026 - 43 Primaries by Postcode
solihull.seoDescription: Solihull area catchment finder: 43 primary + 8 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Solihull has 66 schools including 43 primaries and 8 secondaries, administered across two councils — Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council and parts of Birmingham City. With 35 of those schools operating as academies, each setting its own admissions criteria, checking individual policies is essential; the remaining community schools follow the relevant LA's distance-based tiebreaker.

Demand is real: 22 of the 61 schools with published capacity data are at or above capacity. Nineteen schools have a religious character — predominantly Church of England and Catholic — meaning faith criteria sit alongside proximity in their oversubscription pecking order. One selective school in the area requires a test pass before distance comes into play at all.

croydon.seoTitle: Croydon School Catchment Map 2026 - 38 Primaries by Postcode
croydon.seoDescription: Croydon area catchment finder: 38 primary + 11 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Croydon has 64 schools including 38 primaries and 11 secondaries, coordinated mainly by Croydon Council with a small number of schools falling under Sutton's admissions remit. At 64% of schools operating as academies, the landscape is fragmented — each academy sets its own oversubscription criteria, so the order of priority (sibling, faith, distance) can differ sharply between schools on the same street.

Three selective schools — requiring a test pass before distance matters — add another layer to secondary applications. Faith provision covers 10 schools, drawing mainly Catholic and Church of England pupils from wider catchments than local community schools. Croydon publishes its secondary co-ordinated offer on National Offer Day (1 March) and the primary outcome on 16 April each year.

worthing.seoTitle: Worthing School Catchment Map 2026 - 24 Primaries by Postcode
worthing.seoDescription: Worthing area catchment finder: 24 primary + 6 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. West Sussex 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Worthing's 38 schools sit within West Sussex County Council's admissions remit, with catchment boundaries drawn for each of its 24 primary schools based on measured distances from the school gate. Oversubscription at popular primaries such as those near the seafront and in Goring-by-Sea can push offers beyond 1 mile in quieter years, but fell inside 0.8 miles during the 2024 round - so address matters here.

The town's 6 secondary schools include both comprehensive and faith options, and several have their own supplementary information forms for faith criteria. West Sussex publishes its co-ordinated secondary offer on National Offer Day (1 March) and its primary offer on 16 April - use the catchment.school postcode tool to check each school's last-offered distance before applying.

ely.seoTitle: Ely School Catchment Map 2026 - 19 Primaries by Postcode
ely.seoDescription: Ely area catchment finder: 19 primary + 4 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Cambridgeshire 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Ely has 28 schools including 19 primaries and 4 secondaries, all sitting within Cambridgeshire County Council's co-ordinated admissions area. The cathedral city's compact geography means school choice is limited: once a popular school is oversubscribed, the nearest alternative can be several miles away into the Fens.

Faith schools are prominent here — 10 of the 28 schools have a religious character, a higher proportion than most market towns of this size. Six schools are currently at or above capacity, so catchment distances at oversubscribed primaries can be tighter than parents expect. Cambridgeshire publishes last-distance-offered figures in its annual admissions booklet, usually released in September for the following academic year.

barnet.seoTitle: Barnet School Catchment Map 2026 - 14 Primaries by Postcode
barnet.seoDescription: Barnet area catchment finder: 14 primary + 5 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.
paragraphs: Barnet has 25 schools in this area including 14 primaries and 5 secondaries, with Barnet Council co-ordinating admissions for community schools. Four academies and five faith schools apply their own criteria, which typically give priority to children attending specified feeder primaries or of the relevant faith denomination.

Distance tiebreakers at Barnet community secondaries are measured from home address to the nearest school entrance. With house prices among the highest in North London, competition for places at the most sought-after schools in this part of the borough is intense, and some catchments cover less than 0.5 km.

rochdale.seoTitle: Rochdale School Catchment Map 2026 - 41 Primaries by Postcode
rochdale.seoDescription: Rochdale area catchment finder: 41 primary + 8 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Greater Manchester 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Rochdale has 64 schools including 41 primaries and 8 secondaries, spread across towns such as Heywood, Middleton and Littleborough. Rochdale Council co-ordinates admissions for community schools, but 26 academies and 19 faith schools (primarily Church of England and Roman Catholic) apply their own criteria.

Oversubscription at popular Rochdale primaries is often settled by straight-line distance, though a number of Roman Catholic schools draw pupils from a much wider parish catchment. The council publishes 'last distance offered' data in its annual admissions booklet, usually released in October.

bourne.seoTitle: Bourne School Catchment Map 2026 - 6 Primaries by Postcode
bourne.seoDescription: Bourne area catchment finder: 6 primary + 2 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Lincolnshire 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bourne has 10 schools including 6 primaries and 2 secondaries in Lincolnshire. Nine of the ten schools operate as academies, meaning each sets its own admissions criteria - though in practice most follow the LA's standard distance-based tiebreaker for oversubscription.

Bourne Grammar School is partially selective and requires the Lincolnshire 11+ transfer test, so parents of children approaching Year 6 should register for the test by the deadline in June. For non-selective secondary places, Bourne Community College allocates via Lincolnshire's co-ordinated scheme.

abingdon.seoTitle: Abingdon School Catchment Map 2026 - 21 Primaries by Postcode
abingdon.seoDescription: Abingdon area catchment finder: 21 primary + 3 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Oxfordshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.
paragraphs: Abingdon-on-Thames has 32 schools within Oxfordshire County Council's admissions area - 21 primaries and 3 secondaries, with a strong Church of England sector that operates supplementary faith criteria. The town's growth along the A34 corridor has increased pressure on places in the newer residential areas south of the town centre.

The three secondary schools - Larkmead, John Mason and Fitzharrys - are all comprehensive 11-18 schools and serve distinct parts of the town. Oxfordshire's co-ordinated scheme requires secondary preferences by October and primary preferences by January; families in the Vale of White Horse area closest to Didcot should also compare schools in that town.

sunbury-on-thames.seoTitle: Sunbury-on-Thames School Catchment Map 2026 - 6 Primaries by Postcode
sunbury-on-thames.seoDescription: Sunbury-on-Thames catchment finder: 6 primary + 3 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Surrey 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Sunbury-on-Thames sits within Surrey County Council's admissions area, with 11 schools covering both the original town centre and the newer Sunbury Cross and Lower Sunbury districts. Surrey uses straight-line distance as the final tiebreaker at all community primaries, and in Sunbury - where primary rolls are capped and new capacity has not kept pace with housing growth - last-offered distances at the most popular schools have historically been under 0.6 miles.

Three secondary schools primarily serve the area: Sunbury Manor, Halliford and - for families on the Thames-side stretch - Matthew Arnold in Staines. All are comprehensive. Surrey co-ordinates secondary offers through its online application system, with the deadline for secondary preferences in October and primary preferences in November.

sutton-coldfield.seoTitle: Sutton Coldfield School Catchment Map 2026 - 31 Primaries by Postcode
sutton-coldfield.seoDescription: Sutton Coldfield area catchment finder: 31 primary + 8 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Birmingham 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Sutton Coldfield's 42 schools are administered by Birmingham City Council, whose Primary and Secondary Determined Admission Arrangements set out the oversubscription criteria for each school. The town's 31 primaries span the full spectrum from heavily oversubscribed Church of England schools in the town centre to newer community schools in developments along Mere Green Road and New Hall, where distances offered can be considerably longer.

Eight secondary schools serve the area, including Plantsbrook, Bishop Vesey's Grammar (selective - 11-plus required) and Sutton Coldfield Grammar School for Girls (also selective). Families in the SK4-B73-B76 postcode corridor should apply to Birmingham's co-ordinated scheme in October for secondary places and in January for primary - late applications drop to a lower priority tier.

sittingbourne.seoTitle: Sittingbourne School Catchment Map 2026 - 26 Primaries by Postcode
sittingbourne.seoDescription: Sittingbourne area catchment finder: 26 primary + 5 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Kent 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.
paragraphs: Sittingbourne has 37 schools including 26 primaries and 5 secondaries, governed by Kent County Council, which operates one of England's largest selective systems. Three grammar schools serve the area, meaning secondary applicants must sit the Kent Test in September of Year 5 — a pass is the prerequisite before distance tiebreakers apply for grammar entry.

Oversubscription pressure is above average: 17 of the 36 schools with capacity data are at or above roll, and nine schools have a religious character adding a faith-priority criterion. For the 23 academies in the area, each publishes its own admissions policy independently of the council — check each school's policy directly alongside Kent's co-ordinated scheme.

welwyn-garden-city.seoTitle: Welwyn Garden City School Catchment Map 2026 - 16 Primaries by Postcode
welwyn-garden-city.seoDescription: Welwyn Garden City catchment finder: 16 primary + 3 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Hertfordshire 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Welwyn Garden City has 23 schools including 16 primaries and 3 secondaries, all within Hertfordshire County Council's co-ordinated admissions area. The town was designed as a planned settlement, and its school estate reflects that — schools are distributed relatively evenly across residential neighbourhoods, which keeps most address-based catchments manageable in size.

Four of the 21 schools with capacity data are oversubscribed, so proximity remains the deciding tiebreaker at popular primaries. Three faith schools operate their own priority criteria. Hertfordshire also has selective grammar provision elsewhere in the county, but the Welwyn Garden City secondary schools are all non-selective comprehensives — distance from home to school is the primary tiebreaker once sibling priority is exhausted.

barrow-in-furness.seoTitle: Barrow-in-Furness School Catchment Map 2026 - 24 Primaries by Postcode
barrow-in-furness.seoDescription: Barrow-in-Furness catchment finder: 24 primary + 3 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Westmorland and Furness 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Barrow-in-Furness has 32 schools administered by Westmorland and Furness Council (formed in April 2023 from the merger of Barrow, Eden and South Lakeland districts). The town's 24 primaries serve distinct residential zones - Walney Island, Ormsgill, Hawcoat and the town centre - and many are undersubscribed, meaning most applicants living reasonably close receive a place at their preferred school.

Three secondary schools dominate the secondary sector: Barrow Sixth Form College feeds from Thorncliffe and Furness Academy, while St Bernard's Catholic High School draws from across the peninsula on faith criteria. Westmorland and Furness publishes its co-ordinated scheme annually; families are advised to name three preferences in October to maximise choice.

flintshire.seoTitle: Schools in Flintshire Catchment 2026 - Postcode Map & List
flintshire.seoDescription: Flintshire area catchment finder: 55 schools, every catchment boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 Welsh admissions criteria, Estyn ratings and distance offered last year - free.
paragraphs: Flintshire has 55 schools spread across towns including Mold, Buckley, Flint and Connah's Quay, all within Flintshire County Council's co-ordinated admissions framework. As a Welsh council, Flintshire provides both Welsh-medium and English-medium education — and the two streams maintain separate catchment areas, so families choosing Welsh-medium provision may find their nearest qualifying school is further away than the closest English-medium option.

Admissions are assessed under the School Admissions Code (Wales) and Estyn inspections replace Ofsted for school quality ratings. Flintshire publishes its co-ordinated offer dates in line with the national Welsh timetable — primary offers are released on 16 April and secondary on 1 March. Check each school's Welsh-medium or English-medium designation before applying, as this determines which catchment boundary applies to your address.

ashbourne.seoTitle: Ashbourne School Catchment Map 2026 - 21 Primaries by Postcode
ashbourne.seoDescription: Ashbourne area catchment finder: 21 primary + 1 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Derbyshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.
paragraphs: Ashbourne is a Derbyshire market town with 22 schools, the vast majority of which are rural primaries in the surrounding villages of the Dove Valley and Ecclesbourne catchment. Derbyshire County Council is the admissions authority for most community schools, while several Church of England primaries follow their own voluntary-aided criteria.

Thomas Alleyne's High School is the sole secondary in the town and draws from a wide rural hinterland - including pupils from Staffordshire parishes just across the county border. Parental preference is strong here: the school is typically oversubscribed by local families, so checking the published last-offered distance in the school's admissions policy is important for families moving to the area.

barton-upon-humber.seoTitle: Barton-upon-Humber School Catchment Map 2026 - 4 Primaries by Postcode
barton-upon-humber.seoDescription: Barton-upon-Humber catchment finder: 4 primary + 1 secondary school mapped to your postcode. North Lincolnshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Barton-upon-Humber is a small North Lincolnshire market town with 6 schools - 4 primaries and 1 secondary - all administered by North Lincolnshire Council. The town sits on the southern bank of the Humber, connected to Hull by the Humber Bridge, and its schools reflect a settled community with relatively stable rolls.

Baysgarth School is the main secondary, serving Barton and the surrounding villages. It is non-selective and typically admits all applicants from its defined catchment area. North Lincolnshire co-ordinates its admissions through its published scheme; applications open in September for the following September's intake.

blaydon-on-tyne.seoTitle: Blaydon-on-Tyne School Catchment Map 2026 - 5 Primaries by Postcode
blaydon-on-tyne.seoDescription: Blaydon-on-Tyne catchment finder: 5 primary + 1 secondary school mapped to your postcode. Gateshead 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Blaydon-on-Tyne has 6 schools - 5 primaries and 1 secondary - with catchment boundaries set by Gateshead Council. Three schools hold faith designations (Roman Catholic) and three operate as academies, so it is worth reading each school's individual admissions policy alongside the council's co-ordinated scheme.

Catchment areas in Blaydon are relatively stable year-on-year, as this is a less densely populated part of Gateshead. However, the Roman Catholic secondary draws pupils from a significantly wider area than the community alternatives, and siblings are always given priority after children with EHC plans.

alresford.seoTitle: Alresford School Catchment Map 2026 - 4 Primaries by Postcode
alresford.seoDescription: Alresford area catchment finder: 4 primary + 1 secondary school mapped to your postcode. Hampshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.
paragraphs: Alresford (also known as New Alresford) is a small Hampshire market town with 6 schools - 4 primaries and Perins Multi-Academy Trust secondary. Hampshire County Council co-ordinates admissions for most community schools, and the town's rural location means the secondary catchment extends across a wide swathe of the Mid-Hants watercress-growing valley.

Perins School is the sole secondary and is consistently well-regarded; it draws pupils from Alresford, Alton, Bishop's Sutton and the surrounding villages. Hampshire's application portal opens in September for secondary preferences (deadline October) and in November for primary preferences (deadline January).

beckenham.seoTitle: Beckenham School Catchment Map 2026 - 11 Primaries by Postcode
beckenham.seoDescription: Beckenham area catchment finder: 11 primary + 5 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Bromley 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Beckenham's 18 schools are administered by the London Borough of Bromley, one of the few London boroughs to retain a selective secondary tier alongside comprehensive schools. Catchment areas for Bromley's community primaries use straight-line distance from home to school, measured by the council's GIS system - in competitive zones near Eden Park and Clock House, last-offered distances at popular primaries can fall below 0.4 miles.

Secondary choices include Langley Park Schools for Boys and Girls, which draw from a wide Bromley catchment, and the partially-selective St Joseph's Academy. Bromley coordinates its secondary offer through the Pan-London Admissions Scheme, with preferences submitted via the council's eAdmissions portal by the October deadline.

norwich.seoTitle: Norwich School Catchment Map 2026 - 142 Primaries by Postcode
norwich.seoDescription: Norwich area catchment finder: 142 primary + 22 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Norfolk 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Norwich is Norfolk's county city and one of the most complex admissions landscapes in the East of England, with 192 schools spanning 142 primaries and 22 secondaries across the city and its immediate fringe. Norfolk County Council is the admissions authority for most community schools, but Norwich has a high proportion of academy and church schools that set their own criteria - checking each school's individual policy is essential.

The secondary sector includes three remaining upper schools operating a middle-school system in parts of Norfolk, alongside standard 11-16 and 11-18 comprehensives. Open-access sixth forms and faith schools add further complexity. Norfolk's co-ordinated scheme requires preferences to be submitted by the October secondary deadline and January primary deadline; the council publishes annual data on last-offered distances for each Norwich school.

preston.seoTitle: Preston School Catchment Map 2026 - 122 Primaries by Postcode
preston.seoDescription: Preston area catchment finder: 122 primary + 22 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Lancashire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.
paragraphs: Preston has 176 schools including 122 primaries and 22 secondaries, primarily coordinated by Lancashire County Council with a small number under the remit of neighbouring councils. The city has one of the highest concentrations of faith schools in the North West — 93 of 176 schools have a religious character, predominantly Roman Catholic and Church of England, meaning faith criteria govern more than half of all admission decisions in the area.

Oversubscription is widespread: 51 of 158 schools with published capacity data are at or above roll. Two selective schools require a test pass for grammar entry. For Roman Catholic schools in particular, parish boundaries often extend well beyond the school's immediate neighbourhood, so families outside the local area may still qualify for a priority place. Lancashire publishes last-distance-offered data in its co-ordinated admissions booklet each autumn.

derby.seoTitle: Derby School Catchment Map 2026 - 107 Primaries by Postcode
derby.seoDescription: Derby area catchment finder: 107 primary + 17 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Derby has 158 schools including 107 primaries and 17 secondaries, spread across Derby City Council and parts of Derbyshire County Council's admissions area. Nearly half the schools — 74 — operate as academies with their own individual criteria, making it essential to check each school's policy rather than assuming a uniform distance-based tiebreaker applies across the city.

Thirty schools have a religious character, mainly Church of England and Catholic, adding faith priority to their oversubscription criteria. Pressure on places is notable: 38 of 141 schools with capacity data are at or above roll. Two selective schools in the wider Derby area require a grammar test pass. Both Derby City and Derbyshire publish last-offered-distance data in their respective annual admissions booklets, typically available from September.

loughborough.seoTitle: Loughborough School Catchment Areas 2026 - 38 Primary & 8 Secondary
loughborough.seoDescription: Loughborough catchment finder: 55 Leicestershire schools - 38 primary + 8 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.
paragraphs: Loughborough has 55 schools including 38 primaries and 8 secondaries, straddling the border between Leicestershire County Council and Nottinghamshire County Council — so a small number of schools in the outer areas fall under a different co-ordinated admissions scheme to those in the town centre. The university town's growing population has maintained steady demand for primary places, particularly in newer residential developments to the south and east.

Eighteen of the 55 schools have a religious character, a higher proportion than many comparable market towns, with Catholic and Church of England schools both represented. Seven schools are currently at or above capacity. No selective schools operate in the Loughborough area, so distance-based tiebreakers (measured as a straight line from home to school gate) are the primary differentiator once sibling priority is applied.

eastleigh.seoTitle: Eastleigh School Catchment Areas 2026 - 22 Primary & 4 Secondary | Hampshire
eastleigh.seoDescription: Eastleigh catchment finder: 30 Hampshire schools - 22 primary + 4 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.
paragraphs: Eastleigh has 30 schools - 22 primaries and 4 secondaries - with catchment boundaries set by Hampshire County Council. The town's rapid residential growth means that catchment boundaries at several popular primaries have contracted in recent years as more families compete for places.

Hampshire uses a straight-line distance tiebreaker at community schools after siblings, looked-after children and special-needs allocations. For secondary schools, check whether your postcode falls within the published catchment area before the October deadline, as out-of-catchment applicants are rarely successful at the most popular schools.

colchester.seoTitle: Colchester School Catchment Areas 2026 - 73 Primary & 15 Secondary | Essex
colchester.seoDescription: Colchester catchment finder: 103 Essex schools - 73 primary + 15 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year - free.
paragraphs: Colchester is Essex's largest town and has 103 schools including 73 primaries and 15 secondaries. Essex County Council co-ordinates admissions, but 44 academies and 29 faith schools (Church of England, Roman Catholic and Christian) each publish their own oversubscription criteria alongside the LA's annual admissions booklet.

Demand is particularly acute for secondary places in the Lexden and Stanway areas, where popular schools routinely fill on distance within a mile or less. Colchester's rapid housing development has pushed several primary catchments below 500 metres at their tightest point, so re-checking boundaries annually is essential.

chorley.seoTitle: Chorley School Catchment Areas 2026 - 40 Primary & 5 Secondary | Lancashire
chorley.seoDescription: Chorley catchment finder: 54 Lancashire schools - 40 primary + 5 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.
paragraphs: Chorley is a large Lancashire town with 54 schools - 40 primaries and 5 secondaries - making it one of the busiest admissions zones in the county. Lancashire County Council co-ordinates all maintained school admissions in Chorley, with catchment areas for community primaries drawn on historical boundaries that do not always align with current residential development patterns.

The town's secondary sector includes Southlands High School, Albany Academy and Parklands High School, which together serve most of Chorley's residential zones. Lancashire operates a three-school preference system for secondary admissions, with the deadline in October; primary applications close in mid-January. Oversubscription is most acute at Church of England primaries in the older village areas.

clitheroe.seoTitle: Clitheroe School Catchment Areas 2026 - Grammar & Comprehensive Guide
clitheroe.seoDescription: Clitheroe catchment finder: 23 Lancashire schools including Clitheroe Royal Grammar - 16 primary + 3 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria and Ofsted ratings - free.
paragraphs: Clitheroe has 23 schools including 16 primaries and 3 secondaries in Lancashire's Ribble Valley. Fourteen of those schools carry a faith designation - predominantly Church of England - reflecting the area's strong historic ties to Anglican and United Reformed Church congregations.

Clitheroe Royal Grammar School is a selective grammar, so Year 6 parents must sit Lancashire's 11+ test to be considered. For non-selective secondary places, Lancashire County Council co-ordinates admissions and applies a distance-from-school-gate tiebreaker at oversubscribed community secondaries.

eastbourne.seoTitle: Eastbourne School Catchment Areas 2026 - 19 Primary & 5 Secondary | East Sussex
eastbourne.seoDescription: Eastbourne catchment finder: 35 East Sussex schools - 19 primary + 5 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.
paragraphs: Eastbourne has 35 schools including 19 primaries and 5 secondaries, administered by East Sussex County Council. The town has a high proportion of academies (22 out of 35) which each set their own admissions policies independently of the local authority.

For primary places in Eastbourne, the main oversubscription tiebreaker at community schools is straight-line distance after special-needs and looked-after children have been allocated. Secondary applicants should note that all five main secondaries are academies or academy trusts, so parents need to read each school's prospectus individually to understand catchment or feeder-school criteria.

burnley.seoTitle: Burnley School Catchment Areas 2026 - 34 Primary & 5 Secondary | Lancashire
burnley.seoDescription: Burnley catchment finder: 61 Lancashire schools - 34 primary + 5 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year - free.
paragraphs: Burnley has 61 schools including 34 primaries and 5 secondaries administered by Lancashire County Council. With 19 faith schools across Church of England and Roman Catholic denominations, Burnley has one of the higher proportions of religiously-designated schools among Lancashire's market towns.

At oversubscribed Burnley community schools, Lancashire uses distance measured along the nearest available walking route rather than straight-line distance - a distinction that can affect who falls just inside or outside a catchment. Secondary places at the town's grammar-stream schools are allocated nationally through Lancashire's grammar co-ordination process.

bridlington.seoTitle: Bridlington School Catchment Areas 2026 - 11 Primary & 2 Secondary Schools
bridlington.seoDescription: Bridlington catchment finder: 14 East Riding of Yorkshire schools - 11 primary + 2 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.
paragraphs: Bridlington has 14 schools including 11 primaries and 2 secondaries, all within East Riding of Yorkshire Council's co-ordinated admissions area. As a coastal market town, the school estate is smaller than many urban centres of comparable population, and most families have a limited choice of secondaries — Headlands School and Bridlington School together serve the vast majority of pupils in the town.

One school is currently at or above published capacity, and two schools have a religious character applying faith criteria as part of their oversubscription tiebreaker. East Riding publishes last-distance-offered figures in its annual admissions booklet each autumn, and the council's co-ordinated secondary offer aligns with the national offer date of 1 March.

dukinfield.seoTitle: Dukinfield School Catchment Areas 2026 - Tameside Schools Postcode Map
dukinfield.seoDescription: Dukinfield catchment finder: 12 Tameside schools - 6 primary + 2 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.
paragraphs: Dukinfield has 12 schools including 6 primaries and 2 secondaries, all within Tameside Metropolitan Borough Council's co-ordinated admissions area in Greater Manchester. Nine of the 12 schools operate as academies — a high proportion for a town of this size — meaning each has its own oversubscription criteria, though most still use a distance-based tiebreaker after sibling and faith priority.

Capacity pressure is significant: 6 of the 10 schools with published data are at or above roll, giving Dukinfield one of the higher oversubscription rates in Tameside. Three schools have a religious character, mainly Catholic, drawing from a wider parish catchment than the immediate neighbourhood. Tameside publishes its co-ordinated primary offer on 16 April and secondary offer on 1 March, with last-distance-offered data available in the council's admissions booklet each September.

Kenilworth has 10 schools including 7 primaries and 1 secondary, with catchment boundaries administered by Warwickshire County Council. Three schools operate as Church of England or Roman Catholic faith schools with their own admissions criteria that sit alongside the council's published distance-based policy.

For secondary admissions in Kenilworth, the main oversubscription criterion at community schools is straight-line distance from home to school gate. Parents often find that catchments shift year-on-year depending on application volumes, so checking the previous three years' 'last distance offered' figures is strongly recommended.

Enfield has 50 schools - 32 primaries, 10 secondaries and 8 all-through or special schools. Enfield Council administers community school catchments, while the borough's 16 academies and 12 faith schools (Church of England and Roman Catholic) set their own oversubscription criteria.

Secondary catchment boundaries in Enfield are among the tightest in North London, particularly for schools close to the A10 corridor. Distance to the school gate is the main tiebreaker at community schools; siblings already on roll take priority in round one.

Godalming has 24 schools including 13 primaries and 2 secondaries - all falling under Surrey County Council admissions co-ordination. Of those, 10 are academies or free schools and 10 have a faith designation, making Godalming one of the more complex admissions landscapes in Surrey.

The two main secondary schools in Godalming are Rodborough and Broadwater, both of which use Surrey's standard oversubscription criteria. Demand at both schools means that distance tiebreakers can be decisive; parents living north of the A3100 should check which school's catchment boundary their address falls within.

Epsom has 29 schools - 19 primaries and 4 secondaries - with admissions co-ordinated by Surrey County Council. Nineteen of the 29 schools operate as academies, and 5 carry a faith designation (Roman Catholic and Church of England), so parents should check each school's published admissions policy individually.

Epsom's secondary schools, including Blenheim High School and Rosebery School, allocate oversubscription places primarily by distance. The area is highly sought-after and some popular primaries have seen their last-offered distance fall below 0.6 km - checking the previous year's admissions data before applying is strongly advised.

Esher has 8 schools including 4 primaries and 2 secondaries, with Surrey County Council co-ordinating admissions. The area has a mix of community schools, Church of England schools and academies, each applying its own oversubscription criteria.

Demand for places at Esher's two secondary schools is high. Esher Church of England High School prioritises practising Church of England families, while Hinchley Wood School allocates on distance. Parents living near the boundary between the two catchments should verify their closest school before submitting a preference.

Fareham has 40 schools including 27 primaries and 5 secondaries, with catchment boundaries set by Hampshire County Council. The borough has grown significantly with new housing in Whiteley and Welborne, which has added pressure to several primary school catchments in recent years.

Hampshire's secondary admissions use a traditional catchment area model for community schools: pupils living within the designated catchment have priority after siblings and EHC-plan children. For secondary schools in Fareham, published catchment maps are updated every autumn in Hampshire's 'Apply for a School Place' guide.

Hyde has 22 schools including 16 primaries and 3 secondaries, administered by Tameside Metropolitan Borough Council. Nineteen schools operate as academies - one of the highest academy proportions among Greater Manchester towns - so parents need to consult each school's admissions policy alongside the council's co-ordinated scheme.

Oversubscription at Hyde's community schools is resolved by distance from home to school gate. Roman Catholic and Church of England schools in the area use faith-criteria alongside distance, and typically require evidence of regular worship from the relevant parish or diocese.

Malvern has 22 schools including 14 primaries and 2 secondaries, with admissions overseen by Herefordshire Council. Eleven schools are academies and 11 carry a faith designation (predominantly Church of England and Roman Catholic), giving Malvern one of the more complex admissions mixes for a mid-sized market town.

The main secondary schools serving Malvern are Dyson Perrins C of E Academy and The Chase Technology College. Dyson Perrins gives priority to Church of England worshippers before distance, while The Chase uses straight-line distance as its primary tiebreaker. Parents should check the published catchment maps annually as boundary shifts can affect eligibility.

Okehampton has 12 schools including 10 primaries and 1 secondary - Okehampton College - with admissions co-ordinated by Devon County Council. Nine of the twelve schools operate as academies, largely reflecting the national academy conversion trend in Devon's rural areas.

The primary schools around Okehampton typically serve clearly defined village catchments, meaning most children attend their nearest school without needing to apply through the oversubscription process. Okehampton College, as the sole secondary, admits all children from its defined catchment area before considering distance for out-of-catchment applicants.

Olney has 3 primary schools with admissions co-ordinated by Milton Keynes Council. All three schools operate as academies. There are no secondary schools within Olney itself; the nearest are in Newport Pagnell and Milton Keynes city, served by Milton Keynes's secondary transfer process.

Primary places in Olney are competitive during years of high birth cohorts. Milton Keynes Council uses straight-line distance as the tiebreaker for community academies in the town. Parents planning ahead should note that feeder school links to Newport Pagnell's secondary schools may give priority to Year 6 children at Olney primary academies.

london.seoTitle: London School Catchment Map 2026 - 994 Primaries by Postcode
london.seoDescription: London area catchment finder: 994 primary + 247 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Boroughs set their own 2026 admissions criteria - compare Ofsted ratings and last-distance-offered across Inner and Outer London.
paragraphs: London has over 1,800 schools spread across 32 boroughs and the City of London, making it by far the largest and most complex admissions landscape in England. Each borough operates as its own local authority - so catchment boundaries, oversubscription criteria and distances offered vary sharply between, for example, Barnet in the north and Southwark in the south.

In heavily oversubscribed Inner London areas, the last distance offered at popular primary schools can fall below 500 metres; in Outer London boroughs such as Bromley or Havering, distances of 1-2 km are more common. Faith schools - Church of England, Roman Catholic and Jewish - make up a significant proportion of popular schools and may draw pupils from across borough boundaries.

To search catchment areas for a specific London borough, use the council pages on catchment.school or enter your postcode in the search tool. Always cross-check with the individual school's 2026 admissions policy, as academies set their own criteria independently of the borough.

birmingham.seoTitle: Birmingham School Catchment Map 2026 - 301 Primaries by Postcode
birmingham.seoDescription: Birmingham area catchment finder: 301 primary + 85 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Birmingham City Council 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Birmingham has 517 schools, including 301 primaries and 85 secondaries, coordinated primarily by Birmingham City Council - the largest local authority by population in England. The city's admissions system covers a mix of community schools (using council-set criteria), academies, and a substantial number of faith schools representing Church of England, Roman Catholic, Islamic and other denominations.

Catchment distances at popular Birmingham primaries in areas such as Moseley, Harborne and Sutton Coldfield can be tight, often under 800 metres for the nearest-school tiebreaker. Selective grammar schools in the wider West Midlands area add a further layer to secondary school planning for some families.

Birmingham's admissions round opens each September for the following academic year. Families are advised to list all preferences carefully and to check whether faith school criteria apply, as around a third of Birmingham's schools are faith-designated.

manchester.seoTitle: Manchester School Catchment Map 2026 - 285 Primaries by Postcode
manchester.seoDescription: Manchester area catchment finder: 285 primary + 61 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Manchester, Salford and Trafford 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: The greater Manchester area has around 414 schools in the catchment.school database, spanning Manchester City Council (202 schools), Salford (60), Trafford (43) and other neighbouring authorities. Admissions criteria differ between councils, so a school just across the boundary into Salford or Trafford may use different tiebreakers than a Manchester City school on the same street.

Manchester City Council coordinates admissions for its community and voluntary-controlled schools. Many popular primaries in areas such as Didsbury, Chorlton and Fallowfield are heavily oversubscribed, with last-distance-offered sometimes falling below 600 metres. The city also has a large number of academy schools that set their own admissions policies.

The Greater Manchester Combined Authority does not coordinate school admissions; families must apply through whichever local authority the school is physically located in. Check the relevant council page on catchment.school to see the right authority for your target school.

bristol.seoTitle: Bristol School Catchment Map 2026 - 219 Primaries by Postcode
bristol.seoDescription: Bristol area catchment finder: 219 primary + 42 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Bristol City, South Gloucestershire and North Somerset 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bristol and its surrounding areas have 320 schools in the catchment.school database, split across Bristol City Council (164 schools), South Gloucestershire (106) and North Somerset (27). Families living near the council boundaries in areas such as Filton, Kingswood or Nailsea should pay close attention to which authority a school falls under, as admissions criteria differ.

Within Bristol City, popular primaries in areas such as Redland, Clifton and Stoke Bishop are consistently oversubscribed, with distance tiebreakers sometimes falling below 700 metres. Bristol operates a Fair Banding system for some secondary schools to ensure a broad intake, which changes how secondary admissions work compared to purely distance-based systems.

Bristol's coordinated admissions round runs from September; secondary applications typically close in October for Year 7 entry. Check Bristol City Council's published admissions policy alongside each school's own prospectus, particularly for academy and faith schools.

nottingham.seoTitle: Nottingham School Catchment Map 2026 - 225 Primaries by Postcode
nottingham.seoDescription: Nottingham area catchment finder: 225 primary + 42 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Nottingham City, Nottinghamshire and Derbyshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: The Nottingham area spans 307 schools across Nottingham City Council (114 schools), Nottinghamshire County (166) and parts of Derbyshire (24). The city boundary is a key dividing line: schools in West Bridgford, Arnold or Carlton sit in Nottinghamshire, not Nottingham City - each with their own admissions criteria.

Nottingham City coordinates admissions for community schools within the city boundary. Some popular primaries in areas such as Wollaton, Mapperley and West Bridgford attract applications from a wide catchment, with distance tiebreakers of under a mile at the most sought-after schools. Nottinghamshire County also operates selective grammar schools in nearby towns such as Nottingham, Beeston and Hucknall.

Nottinghamshire maintains a selective secondary school system for some areas - families considering grammar schools should note that the 11-plus test registration deadline differs from the main admissions round. Check each school's individual admissions policy on catchment.school for current 2026 criteria.

liverpool.seoTitle: Liverpool School Catchment Map 2026 - 187 Primaries by Postcode
liverpool.seoDescription: Liverpool area catchment finder: 187 primary + 42 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Liverpool City, Sefton and Knowsley 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Liverpool and the wider Merseyside area have 292 schools across Liverpool City Council (188), Sefton (61) and Knowsley (41). Families in suburbs such as Crosby, Maghull or Kirkby should check which local authority their target school falls under, as admissions policies differ significantly between councils.

Liverpool has a high proportion of faith schools - Roman Catholic schools in particular are numerous and popular across the city. Faith criteria are applied before distance, meaning practising Catholic families may be prioritised at oversubscribed Catholic schools regardless of how close they live. Anglicans and families of other faiths should check individual school admissions policies carefully.

Liverpool City Council's coordinated admissions round opens in September; the secondary transfer deadline is typically in late October. Popular primaries in areas such as Woolton, Mossley Hill and Childwall can have limited places for children outside faith criteria, making early and accurate applications essential.

leeds.seoTitle: Leeds School Catchment Map 2026 - 187 Primaries by Postcode
leeds.seoDescription: Leeds area catchment finder: 187 primary + 32 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Leeds City Council 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Leeds has 258 schools, with 250 falling under Leeds City Council - one of the largest urban local authorities in England. The remainder sit within North Yorkshire or Bradford. Leeds uses straight-line distance as the main tiebreaker for most community schools, but faith schools and academies may apply their own priority criteria first.

Popular primary schools in areas such as Roundhay, Horsforth and Alwoodley are consistently oversubscribed; last-distance-offered at the most sought-after schools can fall below 800 metres. At secondary level, schools such as those in the Chapel Allerton and Headingley areas attract wide competition, with careful postcode research recommended before applications are submitted.

Leeds City Council publishes its composite admissions guide each September, outlining the tiebreaker criteria and previous year's distance data for all community schools. Families are encouraged to list all six preferences on their common application form to maximise chances of a local school offer.

sheffield.seoTitle: Sheffield School Catchment Map 2026 - 166 Primaries by Postcode
sheffield.seoDescription: Sheffield area catchment finder: 166 primary + 32 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Sheffield City Council 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Sheffield has 233 schools in the catchment.school database, primarily within Sheffield City Council (190 schools), with Rotherham (26) and Derbyshire (10) providing the remainder at the city's edges. Sheffield City Council coordinates admissions for community schools; academies and voluntary-aided faith schools operate their own criteria.

Sheffield is notable for its mix of urban and semi-rural areas - schools in suburbs such as Ecclesall, Dore and Fulwood often draw from a comparatively large geographical area, while inner-city schools in areas such as Burngreave or Darnall may be allocated primarily to the immediate neighbourhood. Distance tiebreakers vary considerably across the city.

Sheffield does not operate a selective grammar school system, so secondary admissions are based on distance and, for faith schools, religious affiliation. Families considering church schools should obtain a Supplementary Information Form (SIF) from the school in addition to the local authority application.

leicester.seoTitle: Leicester School Catchment Map 2026 - 153 Primaries by Postcode
leicester.seoDescription: Leicester area catchment finder: 153 primary + 33 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Leicester City and Leicestershire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Leicester and the surrounding area have 225 schools split between Leicester City Council (134 schools) and Leicestershire County Council (91). The city boundary is significant: schools in Oadby, Birstall or Wigston sit in Leicestershire and are coordinated by the county, not the city, with different admissions criteria.

Leicester City has a diverse school landscape with a high proportion of schools with a faith character, including Church of England, Roman Catholic and Hindu-ethos schools. Popular community primaries in areas such as Aylestone, Clarendon Park and Western Park see consistent oversubscription, with distance tiebreakers that can be under a mile at the most popular schools.

Leicestershire County operates selective grammar schools in market towns such as Hinckley, Market Harborough and Loughborough, which attract applicants from across the county. Families in the Leicester suburbs weighing grammar options should note that 11-plus registration closes separately from the main admissions round.

stoke-on-trent.seoTitle: Stoke-on-Trent School Catchment Map 2026 - 121 Primaries by Postcode
stoke-on-trent.seoDescription: Stoke-on-Trent area catchment finder: 121 primary + 25 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Stoke-on-Trent City Council and Staffordshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Stoke-on-Trent has 184 schools in the catchment.school database, with 114 in Stoke-on-Trent City Council's area, 61 in Staffordshire and a small number in Cheshire East. The city is a conurbation of six towns - Burslem, Fenton, Hanley, Longton, Stoke and Tunstall - each with its own cluster of schools spread across a relatively compact geography.

Stoke-on-Trent City Council uses straight-line distance as the primary tiebreaker for community schools. Because the city is densely served by schools, most families can access several primaries within walking distance. However, schools close to popular residential areas in Trentham, Penkhull and Hartshill do see stronger competition for places.

Staffordshire County schools just outside the city boundary - for example, in Newcastle-under-Lyme or Cheadle - have their own admissions policies and should not be confused with the Stoke-on-Trent Council schools. Families near the boundary should check both council pages on catchment.school.

bradford.seoTitle: Bradford School Catchment Map 2026 - 108 Primaries by Postcode
bradford.seoDescription: Bradford area catchment finder: 108 primary + 25 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Bradford Metropolitan District 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bradford has 163 schools, the vast majority (158) within Bradford Metropolitan District Council, which covers the city itself as well as smaller towns such as Ilkley, Keighley, Bingley and Shipley. Bradford MDC uses a complex admissions system that includes feeder school links for some secondary schools, as well as faith, sibling and distance criteria.

Bradford is home to a large number of Church of England and Roman Catholic schools, as well as several Islamic faith schools, making faith criteria a significant factor in admissions decisions across the district. Families should check whether their target school is faith-designated and obtain a supplementary information form if needed.

At primary level, oversubscription tends to be concentrated in the Wharfedale towns such as Ilkley, Ben Rhydding and Burley in Wharfedale, where demand for places is high relative to the number of schools. In the city centre and surrounding areas, schools are generally more accessible.

southampton.seoTitle: Southampton School Catchment Map 2026 - 109 Primaries by Postcode
southampton.seoDescription: Southampton area catchment finder: 109 primary + 22 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Southampton City Council and Hampshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Southampton has 158 schools split between Southampton City Council (84 schools) and Hampshire County Council (74). Schools in suburbs such as Totton, Hedge End or Eastleigh fall under Hampshire, not Southampton City, with distinct admissions criteria. Families close to the authority boundary should verify which council coordinates their target school.

Southampton City Council uses straight-line distance as the primary tiebreaker for community schools. Some popular primaries in areas such as Portswood, Bitterne and Shirley are consistently oversubscribed. Hampshire operates a designated catchment area system for many of its community schools, meaning your address may correspond to a specific school.

Hampshire County Council designates catchment areas for most of its community primary and secondary schools, so families in the Hampshire portion of the Southampton conurbation should check their catchment school via the Hampshire admissions portal. Southampton City uses an open enrolment model without formal catchment boundaries.

reading.seoTitle: Reading School Catchment Map 2026 - 102 Primaries by Postcode
reading.seoDescription: Reading area catchment finder: 102 primary + 21 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Reading Borough Council, Wokingham and West Berkshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Reading has 157 schools across Reading Borough Council (70), Wokingham (37) and West Berkshire (37). The Thames and council boundaries subdivide the area in ways that matter for admissions: schools in Earley, Woodley and Winnersh are in Wokingham; Caversham and the south bank of the Thames are in Reading Borough; while Purley-on-Thames is in West Berkshire.

Reading Borough Council coordinates admissions for its community schools using straight-line distance. Popular primaries in areas such as Caversham Heights, Emmer Green and Tilehurst are frequently oversubscribed. At secondary level, families in the wider Reading area have access to non-selective schools in all three authorities, as well as grammar schools in Berkshire - Grammar School at Leeds and Reading School are among the selective options.

Berkshire operates grammar schools that draw from across the county. Families in the Reading area considering grammar school entry should note that the Berkshire 11-plus registration deadline is in June, well ahead of the main secondary admissions round. Distance tiebreakers at non-selective Reading secondaries can be competitive.

newcastle-upon-tyne.seoTitle: Newcastle upon Tyne School Catchment Map 2026 - 102 Primaries by Postcode
newcastle-upon-tyne.seoDescription: Newcastle upon Tyne area catchment finder: 102 primary + 16 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Newcastle City, North Tyneside and Gateshead 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Newcastle upon Tyne and its immediate environs have 152 schools across Newcastle City Council (111), North Tyneside (22) and Gateshead (10). The River Tyne and the council boundary divide Newcastle from Gateshead; schools on the south bank - including those in Low Fell, Teams and Dunston - are in Gateshead, not Newcastle.

Newcastle City Council coordinates admissions for community schools using straight-line distance. Schools in the West End, Jesmond and Gosforth areas see varying levels of demand; Gosforth in particular has popular schools where distance tiebreakers can be competitive. North Tyneside Council, covering areas such as Whitley Bay, Wallsend and Tynemouth, runs a separate admissions round.

Newcastle upon Tyne has no selective grammar schools; secondary admissions are based on distance, sibling and, for faith schools, religious criteria. The city has a number of Roman Catholic and Church of England schools that give priority to practising families.

doncaster.seoTitle: Doncaster School Catchment Map 2026 - 108 Primaries by Postcode
doncaster.seoDescription: Doncaster area catchment finder: 108 primary + 19 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Doncaster Metropolitan Borough Council 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Doncaster has 151 schools across a large metropolitan borough that includes the town centre as well as towns such as Mexborough, Thorne, Conisbrough and Armthorpe. Doncaster Metropolitan Borough Council (DMBC) coordinates admissions for community schools; academies, which form a significant proportion of Doncaster's secondary schools, apply their own admissions policies.

Doncaster operates a defined feeder primary school system for some of its secondary schools, meaning that children at certain primaries are given priority at linked secondaries. Families should check whether their primary is a named feeder for any target secondary before completing their preferences.

Most of Doncaster's primaries use straight-line distance as the final tiebreaker. Rural schools across the borough may have smaller cohorts, while schools in Doncaster town centre and in the more suburban southern parishes can see keener competition.

bolton.seoTitle: Bolton School Catchment Map 2026 - 98 Primaries by Postcode
bolton.seoDescription: Bolton area catchment finder: 98 primary + 19 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Bolton Metropolitan Borough Council 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bolton has 148 schools, almost all (143) within Bolton Metropolitan Borough Council. The borough stretches from Farnworth and Kearsley in the south to Horwich and Westhoughton in the west, and Turton and Belmont in the north. Bolton MBC coordinates admissions for community schools; faith schools - particularly Roman Catholic and Church of England - apply their own criteria.

Popular schools in the Lostock, Heaton and Smithills areas see strong demand, with distance tiebreakers occasionally below a mile at the most oversubscribed primaries. At secondary level, Bolton's school landscape includes academies, faith schools and a grammar - the Bolton School, a selective independent, attracts applicants from across the borough.

Bolton MBC publishes the composite prospectus each September, detailing oversubscription criteria and previous distance offered for all community schools. Families applying to faith schools should also submit the school's own supplementary information form (SIF) to be considered under faith criteria.

northampton.seoTitle: Northampton School Catchment Map 2026 - 101 Primaries by Postcode
northampton.seoDescription: Northampton area catchment finder: 101 primary + 12 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. West Northamptonshire Council 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Northampton has 142 schools, the majority (137) under West Northamptonshire Council, which was formed in 2021 when Northamptonshire County Council was restructured. A small number of schools at the edges of the Northampton area fall within North Northamptonshire. West Northamptonshire covers not just Northampton but also Daventry and Towcester.

West Northamptonshire uses straight-line distance as the primary tiebreaker for community schools. Popular primaries in the Kingsthorpe, Hunsbury and Duston suburbs can be oversubscribed, particularly as Northampton has seen significant housing growth in recent years. Families in newly built estates should check whether new schools have been planned or whether existing schools have expanded to serve the area.

Northamptonshire does not operate grammar schools at secondary level. Families moving into the Northampton area from counties with selective systems should note that admissions are purely comprehensive. West Northamptonshire Council publishes its secondary school allocation guidance each autumn.

coventry.seoTitle: Coventry School Catchment Map 2026 - 96 Primaries by Postcode
coventry.seoDescription: Coventry area catchment finder: 96 primary + 23 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. Coventry City Council 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Coventry has 140 schools across Coventry City Council (124), Warwickshire County (12) and Solihull MBC (4). Schools in Kenilworth, Leamington Spa and Balsall Common are in Warwickshire, not Coventry; families near the city boundary should confirm which authority coordinates their preferred school.

Coventry City Council uses distance-based tiebreakers for community schools. Popular primaries in areas such as Earlsdon, Finham and Styvechale - the southern suburbs - see consistent oversubscription, with last distances offered sometimes under 600 metres. Coventry has a number of Roman Catholic and Church of England schools that prioritise practising families.

Coventry is a non-selective city for secondary admissions; all secondaries are comprehensive. However, grammar schools in Warwickshire - particularly in Rugby and Stratford-upon-Avon - are accessible to Coventry families prepared to travel. Warwickshire's grammar school 11-plus registration is typically in May, ahead of the October secondary deadline.

york.seoTitle: York School Catchment Map 2026 - 103 Primaries by Postcode
york.seoDescription: York area catchment finder: 103 primary + 13 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. City of York Council and North Yorkshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: York has 136 schools in the catchment.school database, split between City of York Council (73), North Yorkshire (45) and East Riding of Yorkshire (18). The city boundary is important: schools in villages such as Skelton, Haxby and Wigginton may lie in North Yorkshire rather than the City of York, with correspondingly different admissions criteria.

City of York Council uses straight-line distance as the primary tiebreaker for community schools. York's city-centre schools and those in popular residential suburbs such as Fulford, Rawcliffe and Acomb can see strong competition for places. York has no selective grammar schools; secondary admissions are based on distance and, where relevant, faith criteria.

North Yorkshire County Council operates a designated catchment area system for many of its rural and market-town schools, with each school serving a defined geographical area as the first tiebreaker. Families in the villages east and north of York that fall into East Riding territory should apply through the East Riding admissions portal.

wolverhampton.seoTitle: Wolverhampton School Catchment Map 2026 - 82 Primaries by Postcode
wolverhampton.seoDescription: Wolverhampton area catchment finder: 82 primary + 19 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. City of Wolverhampton Council 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Wolverhampton has 134 schools, with 106 under City of Wolverhampton Council, 24 in Staffordshire and 4 in Shropshire. Schools in Codsall, Pattingham and Wombourne fall under Staffordshire, not Wolverhampton - families near the western or northern city boundary should confirm which authority serves their local schools.

City of Wolverhampton Council uses straight-line distance as the primary tiebreaker for community schools. Popular primaries in areas such as Tettenhall, Penn and Finchfield - the more affluent western and southern suburbs - can see last-offered distances below 800 metres. The city has a significant number of Church of England and Roman Catholic schools that give priority to practising families.

Wolverhampton is a non-selective city for secondary admissions; families seeking selective education in the West Midlands typically look to grammar schools in Walsall, Sutton Coldfield or Shropshire. City of Wolverhampton Council coordinates admissions each September with a secondary deadline in October.

banstead.seoTitle: Banstead School Catchment Map 2026 - 8 Schools by Postcode
banstead.seoDescription: Banstead area catchment finder: 8 schools (6 primary, 1 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Surrey admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Banstead is a commuter village in Surrey with 8 state schools - 6 primary, 1 secondary and 1 all-through provision. Admissions are coordinated by Surrey County Council, which publishes catchment boundaries each September for the following academic year.

Because Banstead borders the London Borough of Sutton, some families near the borough boundary may qualify for cross-boundary applications. Check each school's individual admissions policy carefully, as Surrey applies a nearest-school tiebreaker for community schools.

basingstoke.seoTitle: Basingstoke School Catchment Map 2026 - 58 Schools by Postcode
basingstoke.seoDescription: Basingstoke area catchment finder: 58 schools (42 primary, 7 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Hampshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Basingstoke is one of Hampshire's fastest-growing towns, with 58 state schools including 42 primaries and 7 secondaries. Hampshire County Council coordinates admissions and sets catchment boundaries, which are reviewed annually to reflect the town's ongoing residential development.

New housing estates on Basingstoke's northern and western fringes have led to adjustments in catchment areas in recent years. Families in newly built streets should verify their assigned school directly with Hampshire admissions, as school allocations can change when new phases open.

bishops-stortford.seoTitle: Bishop's Stortford School Catchment Map 2026 - 32 Schools by Postcode
bishops-stortford.seoDescription: Bishop's Stortford catchment finder: 32 schools (24 primary, 6 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Essex admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bishop's Stortford sits on the Essex-Hertfordshire border and draws its 32 state schools from a wide rural catchment, with 24 primaries serving both the town and surrounding villages. Admissions are coordinated by Essex County Council for community schools, while academies and faith schools operate their own criteria.

Families living close to the Hertfordshire boundary sometimes qualify to apply across county lines - check both Essex and Hertfordshire admissions for secondary schools in particular, as Hertfordshire's selective grammar schools in nearby areas attract competitive applications from Bishop's Stortford residents.

boston.seoTitle: Boston School Catchment Map 2026 - 37 Schools by Postcode
boston.seoDescription: Boston area catchment finder: 37 schools (25 primary, 6 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Lincolnshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Boston is a market town and port in south Lincolnshire with 37 state schools, including 25 primaries serving the town and its surrounding fenland villages. Lincolnshire County Council coordinates admissions, applying a nearest-school preference for community schools across the district.

The Boston area has seen significant population growth driven by agricultural and food-processing industries, which has increased demand at several primary schools in recent years. Parents are advised to check the latest 'last distance offered' figures carefully, as oversubscription criteria have tightened at the most popular primaries.

braintree.seoTitle: Braintree School Catchment Map 2026 - 23 Schools by Postcode
braintree.seoDescription: Braintree area catchment finder: 23 schools (19 primary, 3 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Essex admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Braintree is a market town in north Essex with 23 state schools, of which 19 are primaries serving the town and surrounding villages including Bocking and Cressing. Essex County Council administers admissions for community schools, while several local academies set their own criteria.

Braintree's three secondary schools attract applicants from a wide catchment including Witham and Halstead. Parents applying for Year 7 places should note that distance tiebreakers are measured in straight lines, and the 'last distance offered' can vary significantly year on year based on application volumes.

bridgwater.seoTitle: Bridgwater School Catchment Map 2026 - 37 Schools by Postcode
bridgwater.seoDescription: Bridgwater area catchment finder: 37 schools (28 primary, 4 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Somerset admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bridgwater is Somerset's largest town on the River Parrett with 37 state schools - 28 primaries and 4 secondaries. Somerset Council coordinates admissions and publishes catchment maps for community schools annually, with boundaries that extend into rural parishes across the Sedgemoor area.

The Hinkley Point C construction project has brought a significant temporary influx of families to the Bridgwater area, increasing competition for school places at several primaries. Families new to the area should register with Somerset admissions early and check whether their address falls within a defined catchment zone or the open-admissions area.

carlisle.seoTitle: Carlisle School Catchment Map 2026 - 56 Schools by Postcode
carlisle.seoDescription: Carlisle area catchment finder: 56 schools (45 primary, 5 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Cumberland admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Carlisle is the main city of Cumberland - the unitary authority created in 2023 - and its 56 state schools include 45 primaries serving both urban neighbourhoods and a wide rural hinterland extending towards the Scottish border. Cumberland Council coordinates admissions and sets catchment areas, which are reviewed annually.

The large geographic catchment means some village primaries feed into secondary schools in Carlisle city, requiring families to plan transport carefully. Carlisle has three grammar schools that operate selective admissions across Cumberland and the surrounding area, so families should register for the 11-plus test separately if considering selective secondary education.

cheadle.seoTitle: Cheadle School Catchment Map 2026 - 25 Schools by Postcode
cheadle.seoDescription: Cheadle area catchment finder: 25 schools (15 primary, 4 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Stockport admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Cheadle is an affluent suburban town in the Stockport metropolitan borough with 25 state schools, including 15 primaries spread across Cheadle, Cheadle Hulme and surrounding residential areas. Stockport Council coordinates admissions, applying nearest-school and sibling-priority criteria for community schools.

Competition for places at Cheadle's most popular primary schools has increased as the area attracts families relocating from Manchester. Some schools in the Cheadle Hulme area are consistently oversubscribed, with the last distance offered occasionally falling below 500 metres - parents should verify the most recent figures in Stockport's annual admissions booklet.

gosport.seoTitle: Gosport School Catchment Map 2026 - 30 Schools by Postcode
gosport.seoDescription: Gosport area catchment finder: 30 schools (23 primary, 3 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Hampshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Gosport is a peninsular town on Portsmouth Harbour in Hampshire with 30 state schools - 23 primaries and 3 secondaries - serving a densely populated area bordered by water on three sides. Hampshire County Council coordinates admissions, and the town's geography means the catchment is effectively self-contained with limited cross-borough movement.

All three of Gosport's secondary schools are on the peninsula, so Year 7 applications are handled locally through Hampshire's co-ordinated scheme. Families considering schools in nearby Fareham or Lee-on-the-Solent should check Hampshire's transfer guide for the most recent admissions criteria and distance data.

harrogate.seoTitle: Harrogate School Catchment Map 2026 - 52 Schools by Postcode
harrogate.seoDescription: Harrogate area catchment finder: 52 schools (36 primary, 6 secondary) mapped to your postcode. North Yorkshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Harrogate is a spa and conference town in North Yorkshire with 52 state schools - 36 primaries and 6 secondaries - serving the town and a broad rural catchment stretching into Nidderdale and Knaresborough. North Yorkshire Council coordinates admissions and publishes catchment boundaries each year, with rural community schools typically applying a parish or nearest-school preference.

Harrogate's secondary schools are popular and several have been oversubscribed in recent years, with the nearest-school tiebreaker applying after siblings and looked-after children. Families in villages such as Pannal and Spofforth should check which secondary school their address is linked to, as the large geographic area means links are not always intuitive.

hatfield.seoTitle: Hatfield School Catchment Map 2026 - 19 Schools by Postcode
hatfield.seoDescription: Hatfield area catchment finder: 19 schools (11 primary, 3 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Hertfordshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Hatfield is a post-war new town in Hertfordshire with 19 state schools, including 11 primaries spread across distinct residential 'neighbourhoods' built around the de Havilland aircraft works. Hertfordshire County Council coordinates admissions and defines linked junior schools for infant-to-junior transfers specific to the new-town layout.

Three secondary schools serve Hatfield, and Hertfordshire applies a feeder-school preference at the most popular ones. The town's proximity to Welwyn Garden City means some families consider cross-town secondary applications - check Hertfordshire's annual secondary transfer guide for current feeder-school and distance data.

hereford.seoTitle: Hereford School Catchment Map 2026 - 64 Schools by Postcode
hereford.seoDescription: Hereford area catchment finder: 64 schools (42 primary, 8 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Herefordshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Hereford is the only city in Herefordshire and the administrative centre of this predominantly rural county, with 64 state schools including 42 primaries serving the city and a large rural catchment. Herefordshire Council coordinates admissions and publishes annual catchment maps, with many village schools drawing from named parishes.

Hereford's secondary schools include two with sixth forms and strong Ofsted ratings, making them competitive at Year 7. Families in surrounding villages should check whether their address is assigned to a Hereford city secondary or a smaller market-town school elsewhere in the county, as transport arrangements vary significantly by location.

knottingley.seoTitle: Knottingley School Catchment Map 2026 - 9 Schools by Postcode
knottingley.seoDescription: Knottingley area catchment finder: 9 schools (7 primary, 1 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Wakefield admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Knottingley is a former mining and glass-manufacturing town in the Wakefield metropolitan district with 9 state schools - 7 primaries and 1 secondary. Wakefield Council coordinates admissions and applies nearest-school criteria for community schools, with catchment boundaries reviewed annually.

Knottingley's single secondary school, De Lacy Academy, serves the town alongside nearby Ferrybridge and Kellington, drawing from a compact urban catchment. Families should note that Wakefield has no grammar schools, so all secondary provision is comprehensive; oversubscription at De Lacy Academy is resolved using a straight-line distance tiebreaker.

lewes.seoTitle: Lewes School Catchment Map 2026 - 22 Schools by Postcode
lewes.seoDescription: Lewes area catchment finder: 22 schools (15 primary, 3 secondary) mapped to your postcode. East Sussex admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Lewes is the county town of East Sussex, sitting in the South Downs between Brighton and Eastbourne, with 22 state schools including 15 primaries serving the town and surrounding villages such as Ringmer and Ditchling. East Sussex County Council coordinates admissions and publishes catchment maps annually.

Lewes has three secondary schools: two in the town and one serving the Ringmer area. The Lewes schools have been oversubscribed in recent years as families relocate from Brighton and London - parents should check the last-distance-offered data carefully and consider applying to all three secondaries if they live at the edge of the town.

littlehampton.seoTitle: Littlehampton School Catchment Map 2026 - 15 Schools by Postcode
