littlehampton.seoDescription: Littlehampton area catchment finder: 15 schools (12 primary, 2 secondary) mapped to your postcode. West Sussex admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Littlehampton is a coastal town at the mouth of the River Arun in West Sussex with 15 state schools - 12 primaries and 2 secondaries. West Sussex County Council coordinates admissions, applying a nearest-school preference for community primaries and specific feeder arrangements for secondary transfer.

The town's two secondary schools - Littlehampton Academy and Wick CofE - draw from a compact coastal catchment. West Sussex's secondary transfer process uses defined catchment areas, and families in the East Preston and Angmering area may be linked to different secondaries depending on their home postcode, so verification with West Sussex admissions is recommended.

newton-aycliffe.seoTitle: Newton Aycliffe School Catchment Map 2026 - 17 Schools by Postcode
newton-aycliffe.seoDescription: Newton Aycliffe area catchment finder: 17 schools (10 primary, 3 secondary) mapped to your postcode. County Durham admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Newton Aycliffe is a designated post-war new town in County Durham with 17 state schools - 10 primaries and 3 secondaries - planned around the town's distinctive neighbourhood layout. Durham County Council coordinates admissions and has historically assigned primary schools to neighbourhoods, though this is subject to annual review.

Three secondary schools serve Newton Aycliffe: Woodham Academy, Greenfield Academy, and Aycliffe Village Primary converts to secondary status in parts of the area. Durham applies a distance tiebreaker after sibling and looked-after-children preferences; families in the Simpasture and Aycliffe Village areas should confirm which secondary their address is linked to.

peterborough.seoTitle: Peterborough School Catchment Map 2026 - 115 Schools by Postcode
peterborough.seoDescription: Peterborough area catchment finder: 115 schools (82 primary, 14 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Peterborough City Council admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Peterborough is a unitary authority city in Cambridgeshire with 115 state schools - 82 primaries and 14 secondaries - making it one of the largest school networks outside the major metropolitan areas. Peterborough City Council coordinates admissions and publishes annual catchment maps for its community schools; academy trusts in the city set their own criteria.

Peterborough's rapid population growth through inward migration has increased pressure on school places in several areas of the city, particularly in the Paston and Orton estates. The city has several grammar schools that conduct the 11-plus, attracting applications from across Peterborough and from neighbouring Cambridgeshire, so families considering selective education should register early.

sandbach.seoTitle: Sandbach School Catchment Map 2026 - 13 Schools by Postcode
sandbach.seoDescription: Sandbach area catchment finder: 13 schools (9 primary, 2 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Cheshire East admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Sandbach is a market town in Cheshire East known for its Anglo-Saxon crosses and salt-industry heritage, with 13 state schools including 9 primaries and 2 secondaries. Cheshire East Council coordinates admissions for community schools, applying a nearest-school preference as the main tiebreaker.

Sandbach's two secondary schools - Sandbach School (boys) and Sandbach High School and Sixth Form College (mixed) - serve the town and surrounding villages including Elworth and Holmes Chapel. Sandbach School is a selective boys' grammar school that admits via the Cheshire East grammar entrance test, so families considering secondary options should check the selective criteria separately.

stevenage.seoTitle: Stevenage School Catchment Map 2026 - 42 Schools by Postcode
stevenage.seoDescription: Stevenage area catchment finder: 42 schools (29 primary, 6 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Hertfordshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Stevenage was the UK's first designated new town and retains a neighbourhood structure with 42 state schools - 29 primaries and 6 secondaries - organised around the town's residential zones. Hertfordshire County Council coordinates admissions and links primary schools to secondary feeders that reflect the original new-town planning.

Six secondary schools serve Stevenage, and Hertfordshire applies feeder-school preferences at most of them. Families who move into the area partway through primary school may not attend a feeder school and so fall back on a distance tiebreaker for secondary allocation - checking the current feeder-link list via Hertfordshire's admissions portal is strongly advised.

sudbury.seoTitle: Sudbury School Catchment Map 2026 - 24 Schools by Postcode
sudbury.seoDescription: Sudbury area catchment finder: 24 schools (17 primary, 3 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Essex admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Sudbury is a market town on the River Stour at the Suffolk-Essex border with 24 state schools, including 17 primaries serving the town and a wide cluster of surrounding villages. Essex County Council coordinates admissions for community schools in the Essex portion of the catchment, while Suffolk County Council administers schools on the Suffolk side.

Because the area straddles two local authority boundaries, families near Great Cornard or Acton should check which council administers their nearest schools before applying. Sudbury's three secondary schools serve an extensive rural catchment - competition for Year 7 places at the most popular schools can be significant for families more than 3 miles from their preferred school.

watford.seoTitle: Watford School Catchment Map 2026 - 52 Schools by Postcode
watford.seoDescription: Watford area catchment finder: 52 schools (36 primary, 6 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Hertfordshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Watford is a commercial town on the edge of Greater London in Hertfordshire with 52 state schools - 36 primaries and 6 secondaries - serving a densely populated area that includes Bushey, Garston and Leavesden. Hertfordshire County Council coordinates admissions, and the town's compact geography means several primary schools are consistently oversubscribed.

Watford's proximity to London attracts families pricing out of the capital, keeping demand for the most popular primaries high. Several of Watford's secondaries have been graded Outstanding by Ofsted, increasing competition at Year 7. Families should note that some Hertfordshire secondaries use feeder-school preferences, so the primary school chosen may affect secondary allocation.

winchester.seoTitle: Winchester School Catchment Map 2026 - 35 Schools by Postcode
winchester.seoDescription: Winchester area catchment finder: 35 schools (21 primary, 2 secondary) mapped to your postcode. Hampshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Winchester is Hampshire's historic cathedral city and county town, with 35 state schools including 21 primaries serving the city and a broad rural catchment across mid-Hampshire villages such as Itchen Abbas and Kings Worthy. Hampshire County Council coordinates admissions and publishes annual catchment boundaries.

Winchester has only two state secondary schools - Henry Beaufort and Kings' School - for the city's catchment, which creates significant competition at Year 7. Hampshire's secondary admissions use a nearest-school tiebreaker, and the last distance offered at Winchester's secondaries can fall well below 2 miles in competitive years; families in outlying villages should apply to both and consider Eastleigh or Romsey secondaries as alternatives.

cambridge.seoTitle: Cambridge School Catchment Areas 2026 - 127 Schools by Postcode
cambridge.seoDescription: Cambridge area catchment finder: 78 primary + 16 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Cambridgeshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Cambridge has 127 schools across the city and its surrounding villages, administered by Cambridgeshire County Council. The city's mix of community schools, Church of England primaries, and selective grammar schools means admissions criteria vary significantly - some schools prioritise faith, others use strict distance tiebreakers. Popular schools in central Cambridge have historically offered places to children living within 0.5 miles, so checking the latest 'last distance offered' data before applying is essential.

Secondary admissions in Cambridge are particularly competitive. Hills Road Sixth Form College and Chesterton Community College draw applications from across the county, while selective schools require the Cambridgeshire 11+ test. For primary applications, the council's coordinated scheme deadline is typically mid-January for September entry - catchment boundaries are reviewed annually and can shift year to year.

milton-keynes.seoTitle: Milton Keynes School Catchment Areas 2026 - 119 Schools by Postcode
milton-keynes.seoDescription: Milton Keynes area catchment finder: 85 primary + 12 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Milton Keynes has 119 schools across the borough, including 85 primary and 12 secondary schools. As a planned city with distinct housing areas - from Wolverton and Newport Pagnell to the modern grid squares of central MK - catchment boundaries often align with neighbourhood boundaries. Milton Keynes Council coordinates admissions, with most community schools using distance as the main tiebreaker after looked-after children and siblings.

Secondary schools in Milton Keynes include a mix of academies, free schools, and community comprehensives. Stantonbury School and Denbigh School are among the most established, drawing pupils from across the borough. For families in newer developments such as Tattenhoe or Kingsmead, it is worth checking the designated catchment school carefully, as boundaries are updated each year to reflect new housing.

hull.seoTitle: Hull School Catchment Areas 2026 - 117 Schools by Postcode
hull.seoDescription: Hull (Kingston upon Hull) catchment finder: 87 primary + 14 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered.
paragraphs: Hull (Kingston upon Hull) has 117 schools across the city, with 87 primary and 14 secondary schools administered by Hull City Council. The city is structured into distinct neighbourhoods - from Bransholme and Anlaby Road in the north and west to Holderness Road and Longhill in the east - and catchment areas broadly follow these geographic divides. Most community schools use proximity as the key tiebreaker after siblings.

Secondary education in Hull includes a number of high-performing academies. Sirius Academy West and Malet Lambert are among the most sought-after, with demand sometimes exceeding catchment distances of under one mile. Hull has invested significantly in school improvement, and Ofsted judgements across the city have improved markedly since 2019. Families should apply through the council's coordinated scheme by mid-January for September secondary places.

oldham.seoTitle: Oldham School Catchment Areas 2026 - 114 Schools by Postcode
oldham.seoDescription: Oldham area catchment finder: 79 primary + 13 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Oldham has 114 schools across the metropolitan borough, including 79 primary and 13 secondary schools. Oldham Council coordinates admissions for community and voluntary-controlled schools, while academies and voluntary-aided schools manage their own admissions within the same national framework. The borough spans a wide area - from the town centre to outlying settlements like Saddleworth, Shaw, and Lees - and catchment distances reflect population density.

Secondary schools in Oldham include Royton and Crompton Academy and Oldham Academy North among those with strong recent Ofsted judgements. The borough has a high proportion of faith schools at both primary and secondary level, several of which admit pupils from across the borough based on religious criteria rather than proximity. Families should review each school's individual admissions policy alongside the council's composite prospectus when making applications.

stockport.seoTitle: Stockport School Catchment Areas 2026 - 113 Schools by Postcode
stockport.seoDescription: Stockport catchment finder: 76 primary + 11 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Stockport has 113 schools across the metropolitan borough, administered by Stockport Council. The borough stretches from Hazel Grove and Bramhall in the south to Reddish and Heaton Chapel bordering Manchester in the north - and school catchment areas tend to be tighter in more densely populated areas like Edgeley, where primary places are heavily contested. Distance tiebreakers for popular Stockport primaries can be as little as 0.3 miles in some years.

At secondary level, Stockport has a selective grammar school - Stockport Grammar School - alongside a range of academies and community schools. The grammar schools admit by 11+ test and draw from across the borough and neighbouring areas, so non-selective catchment distances for comprehensives can be wider. Schools in sought-after postcodes such as SK7 (Bramhall/Cheadle Hulme) are often oversubscribed, and families should check annual offer data carefully before choosing a home.

plymouth.seoTitle: Plymouth School Catchment Areas 2026 - 113 Schools by Postcode
plymouth.seoDescription: Plymouth catchment finder: 76 primary + 19 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Plymouth has 113 schools across the city, including 76 primary and 19 secondary schools, administered by Plymouth City Council. The city is divided into distinct communities - Devonport, Plymstock, Plympton, Peverell, and St Jude's among them - and catchment areas broadly reflect these neighbourhoods. Most community schools use proximity as the primary tiebreaker, with popular primaries in central and east Plymouth historically offering places within 0.6 miles.

Secondary education in Plymouth includes a strong set of academies. Plymouth School of Creative Arts is a specialist arts academy that attracts applications from across the city, while Devonport High School for Boys and Devonport High School for Girls are selective grammar schools admitting via the Devon 11+ test. The council's coordinated scheme deadline for secondary applications is the national closing date of 31 October each year.

lincoln.seoTitle: Lincoln School Catchment Areas 2026 - 108 Schools by Postcode
lincoln.seoDescription: Lincoln catchment finder: 76 primary + 13 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Lincolnshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Lincoln and its surrounding area has 108 schools, with 76 primary and 13 secondary schools co-ordinated by Lincolnshire County Council. The city has grown rapidly on its southern and western edges, with new housing estates in Birchwood, North Hykeham, and Skellingthorpe increasing pressure on local schools. Catchment boundaries in these growth areas are reviewed annually, and families in newer developments should verify their designated school early.

Secondary education in Lincoln includes both selective and non-selective options. The City of Lincoln Academy and Lincoln UTC are popular non-selective choices, while the county's grammar schools - including Lincoln Minster School and Christ's Hospital School - admit on selective criteria. For families seeking grammar school places, registration deadlines and 11+ test dates fall in the summer term of Year 5, well ahead of the standard admissions timeline.

walsall.seoTitle: Walsall School Catchment Areas 2026 - 107 Schools by Postcode
walsall.seoDescription: Walsall catchment finder: 69 primary + 15 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions tiebreakers, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Walsall has 107 schools across the metropolitan borough, with 69 primary and 15 secondary schools. Walsall Council coordinates admissions for community and voluntary-controlled schools, but the borough has a significant proportion of academies that set their own admissions criteria. Areas such as Streetly, Aldridge, and Brownhills tend to have more oversubscribed schools than the town centre, and popular primaries in these areas have historically offered places within 0.4 miles.

At secondary level, Queen Mary's Grammar School in Walsall town centre is one of the West Midlands' highest-achieving selective schools, drawing applicants from across the borough and beyond via the NFER 11+ test. Non-selective secondary schools in the borough include several outstanding academies. Families should note that Walsall sits within the West Midlands grammar school area, meaning selective places are available without needing to live within a specific catchment boundary.

swindon.seoTitle: Swindon School Catchment Areas 2026 - 106 Schools by Postcode
swindon.seoDescription: Swindon catchment finder: 77 primary + 15 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Swindon has 106 schools across the borough, with 77 primary and 15 secondary schools administered by Swindon Borough Council. The town has expanded rapidly westward into the Wichelstowe and Tadpole Garden Village developments, creating additional pressure on existing schools and prompting new free schools to open. Families buying in newer estates should confirm which school they are linked to - designated catchment schools for new builds are not always the nearest geographically.

Secondary schools in Swindon include Churchfields Academy, Ridgeway School, and Nova Hreod Academy, with Cirencester's selective Deer Park school accessible to some border postcodes. Swindon Borough Council publishes its composite prospectus each autumn with admissions policies for every school, and the national secondary deadline of 31 October applies. Primary school applications close in mid-January for September entry.

bedford.seoTitle: Bedford School Catchment Areas 2026 - 103 Schools by Postcode
bedford.seoDescription: Bedford catchment finder: 66 primary + 14 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bedford has 103 schools across the borough, with 66 primary and 14 secondary schools. Bedford Borough Council coordinates admissions for community schools, while the borough's significant proportion of voluntary-aided and academy schools manage their own criteria. Bedford town has a diverse population - including a large Italian-heritage community in Kempston - and school popularity varies considerably across the borough's neighbourhoods.

Bedford is unusual in retaining upper schools in a three-tier system across parts of the borough, with pupils moving from first school to middle school at Year 5, then to upper school at Year 9. Families new to the area should check carefully whether their postcode falls within the two-tier or three-tier catchment structure. The borough's selective upper school, Bedford Academy, admits via entrance test and draws from across the borough.

warrington.seoTitle: Warrington School Catchment Areas 2026 - 102 Schools by Postcode
warrington.seoDescription: Warrington catchment finder: 77 primary + 14 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Warrington has 102 schools across the borough, with 77 primary and 14 secondary schools administered by Warrington Borough Council. Situated between Manchester and Liverpool, Warrington has grown significantly through planned housing developments in Chapelford, Omega, and South Warrington, increasing demand for local school places. Catchment areas in newer housing zones are carefully monitored and updated annually.

Secondary schools in Warrington include Bridgewater High School, The Grange School, and Cardinal Newman Catholic High School, among others. The borough has a strong Catholic school tradition, with several voluntary-aided primaries and secondaries that admit on faith criteria independently of the council's catchment areas. Families applying for faith school places should contact individual schools directly to understand their supplementary information form requirements.

wigan.seoTitle: Wigan School Catchment Areas 2026 - 101 Schools by Postcode
wigan.seoDescription: Wigan catchment finder: 70 primary + 13 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Wigan metropolitan borough has 101 schools, with 70 primary and 13 secondary schools across towns including Wigan, Leigh, Atherton, and Hindley. Wigan Council coordinates admissions for community and voluntary-controlled schools; most use proximity as the primary tiebreaker after looked-after children and siblings. Catchment areas in Leigh and the eastern townships tend to be larger than in Wigan town centre due to lower population density.

Secondary education in Wigan includes a number of high-performing academies and faith schools. Wigan and Leigh College is a significant post-16 provider drawing from across the borough. Several Catholic secondary schools in the borough admit on faith criteria via the council's coordinated scheme but use their own supplementary information forms. Families should check each school's published admissions policy in the council's composite prospectus, available each autumn.

rotherham.seoTitle: Rotherham School Catchment Areas 2026 - 101 Schools by Postcode
rotherham.seoDescription: Rotherham catchment finder: 76 primary + 13 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Rotherham metropolitan borough has 101 schools, with 76 primary and 13 secondary schools administered by Rotherham Council. The borough spans from the town centre through to Maltby, Dinnington, and the rural parishes of Rother Valley. School improvement has been a significant focus following the council's improvement journey since 2015, and Ofsted judgements across Rotherham's schools have improved substantially in recent years.

Secondary schools in Rotherham include Oakwood High School, Wales High School, and Aston Academy. The borough also has a number of faith schools that use religious criteria for oversubscription. For families relocating to the area, Rotherham's composite prospectus is published each October and includes detailed catchment maps, admissions criteria, and historical 'last distance offered' data for every school in the borough.

ipswich.seoTitle: Ipswich School Catchment Areas 2026 - 98 Schools by Postcode
ipswich.seoDescription: Ipswich catchment finder: 62 primary + 12 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Suffolk admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Ipswich has 98 schools across the town and its surrounding parishes, with 62 primary and 12 secondary schools. Suffolk County Council coordinates admissions for community schools, while the town's academies and faith schools manage their own criteria. Ipswich is Suffolk's county town and largest urban area, with popular primaries in the Rushmere, Whitton, and Clapgate areas historically offering places within 0.5 miles in oversubscribed years.

Secondary education in Ipswich includes Northgate High School, Ormiston Endeavour Academy, and Suffolk New College for post-16 study. Several of Ipswich's secondary schools have been converted to academy status in recent years, meaning they hold their own admissions authority. Suffolk County Council publishes annual admissions data including each school's published admission number and last distance offered - essential reading for families choosing secondary schools.

oxford.seoTitle: Oxford School Catchment Areas 2026 - 95 Schools by Postcode
oxford.seoDescription: Oxford catchment finder: 48 primary + 8 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Oxfordshire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Oxford has 95 schools across the city, with 48 primary and 8 secondary schools. Oxfordshire County Council coordinates admissions for the city's community schools, though many of Oxford's primaries are Church of England voluntary-aided schools that manage their own admissions. The city is split into catchment areas roughly along the axes of the Cowley Road, Headington, Jericho, and Summertown neighbourhoods, with popular schools in north and east Oxford historically receiving more applications than places.

Oxford's eight secondary schools are all non-selective comprehensives - the county retains no grammar schools. Cherwell School, Oxford Spires Academy, and Cheney School are among the most in-demand, with popular schools sometimes offering places to children living within 1 mile. Oxford's large transient academic population (associated with the university) means school rolls can fluctuate; the council's annual admissions data is the most reliable guide to current catchment distances.

middlesbrough.seoTitle: Middlesbrough School Catchment Areas 2026 - 89 Schools by Postcode
middlesbrough.seoDescription: Middlesbrough catchment finder: 61 primary + 11 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Middlesbrough has 89 schools, with 61 primary and 11 secondary schools administered by Middlesbrough Council. The borough covers the town centre and outer suburbs including Marton, Acklam, and Hemlington. School admissions in Middlesbrough are coordinated by the council, with most community schools using proximity as the primary tiebreaker. Catchment areas in more affluent southern suburbs such as Marton tend to be tighter due to higher demand.

Secondary schools in Middlesbrough include Outwood Academy Acklam, Macmillan Academy, and Unity City Academy. The area has seen significant academy conversion since 2010, meaning most secondary schools set their own admissions criteria within the national framework. Middlesbrough is adjacent to Redcar & Cleveland and Stockton-on-Tees, so families close to borough boundaries may wish to consider cross-boundary applications - the council's coordinated scheme accommodates preferences outside Middlesbrough.

gwynedd.seoTitle: Gwynedd School Catchment Areas 2026 - 89 Schools by Postcode
gwynedd.seoDescription: Gwynedd catchment finder: 89 schools across North Wales mapped to your postcode. Welsh-medium and English-medium admissions criteria, Ofsted/Estyn ratings for 2026.
paragraphs: Gwynedd has 89 schools across a large, predominantly rural county in north-west Wales, administered by Gwynedd Council. As a stronghold of the Welsh language, the vast majority of Gwynedd's schools are Welsh-medium - meaning lessons are conducted in Welsh, with English taught as a second language. Families relocating to the county from England or non-Welsh-speaking areas should be aware that their nearest school may well be Welsh-medium, and that English-medium provision in some parts of the county is limited.

School catchment areas in Gwynedd tend to be geographically large, reflecting low population density across Snowdonia and the Llŷn Peninsula. Bangor and Caernarfon are the largest urban centres with the greatest choice of schools. Gwynedd Council's admissions authority is Cyngor Gwynedd, and schools in the county are inspected by Estyn (the Wales education inspectorate) rather than Ofsted. Families should consult both Cyngor Gwynedd's admissions policies and Estyn inspection reports when choosing schools.

swansea.seoTitle: Swansea School Catchment Areas 2026 - 89 Schools by Postcode
swansea.seoDescription: Swansea catchment finder: 89 schools across the city mapped to your postcode. Welsh-medium and English-medium admissions criteria, Estyn ratings for 2026.
paragraphs: Swansea (Abertawe) has 89 schools across the city and its surrounding areas, administered by City and County of Swansea Council. The city offers a mix of Welsh-medium and English-medium schools at both primary and secondary level, making it one of the key centres for Welsh-language education in south Wales. Popular English-medium primaries in Sketty, Uplands, and the city centre tend to be oversubscribed, with proximity and siblings as the main tiebreakers.

Secondary schools in Swansea include Olchfa School, Bishop Gore School, and Gowerton School, the latter serving the Gower Peninsula. The bilingual Welsh medium secondary, Ysgol Gymraeg Bryn Tawe, draws pupils from across the city. Schools in Swansea are inspected by Estyn, and the council's composite prospectus is published each autumn. Families considering Welsh-medium education should note that demand for Welsh-medium places has grown significantly in recent years, and waiting lists can develop even mid-year.

huddersfield.seoTitle: Huddersfield School Catchment Areas 2026 - 88 Schools by Postcode
huddersfield.seoDescription: Huddersfield catchment finder: 63 primary + 9 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Kirklees admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Huddersfield has 88 schools across the town and surrounding townships, with 63 primary and 9 secondary schools administered by Kirklees Council. The borough of Kirklees is one of England's largest metropolitan boroughs, and Huddersfield is its main town. Catchment areas in Huddersfield tend to reflect the town's distinct communities - Lindley, Marsh, Moldgreen, and Lockwood - with popular primaries in western Huddersfield historically offering places within 0.5 miles.

Secondary schools in Huddersfield include Almondbury Community School, Newsome Academy, and North Huddersfield Trust School. The area has a high proportion of academy schools at secondary level. Kirklees Council coordinates admissions and publishes detailed catchment data annually. Families considering grammar school education should note that the West Riding Grammar School in Heckmondwike serves much of Kirklees, with selective places available via the 11+ test to children from across the borough.

gloucester.seoTitle: Gloucester School Catchment Areas 2026 - 88 Schools by Postcode
gloucester.seoDescription: Gloucester catchment finder: 64 primary + 12 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Gloucestershire admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Gloucester has 88 schools across the city and its surrounding parishes, with 64 primary and 12 secondary schools administered by Gloucestershire County Council. The city has seen significant housing growth in Quedgeley, Kingsway, and Innsworth, increasing pressure on popular primary schools. Presdales operates a partially-selective entry for girls showing high ability and draws applicants from well beyond Ware itself; Ware Academy is fully comprehensive and caters primarily to the town and immediate villages. A significant proportion of Luton secondaries are academies, each setting their own admissions criteria, so families should check individual school policies alongside the council's co-ordinated offer. For secondary schools, Spalding Grammar (selective) and Spalding High School (selective girls) serve the town alongside Sir John Gleed School. Selective schools require the Lincolnshire selection test; non-selective places are allocated primarily on catchment distance.

burton-on-trent.seoTitle: Schools in Burton-on-Trent Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
burton-on-trent.seoDescription: Burton-on-Trent catchment area: 45 schools across Burton, Swadlincote and the Staffordshire-Derbyshire border. Admissions boundaries, 2026 criteria and school ratings.
paragraphs: Burton-on-Trent straddles the Staffordshire and Derbyshire border, and its 45 schools are split between two local authorities - Staffordshire County Council and Derbyshire County Council - as well as some East Staffordshire Borough standalone academies. Families should check which authority administers their nearest school before applying.

The town centre and outer suburbs such as Stapenhill, Winshill and Branston each have their own primary feeder schools, with catchment boundaries that generally align with the surrounding residential streets. Secondary schools including Paulet High and de Ferrers Academy are oversubscribed in most years.

Proximity after siblings is the standard tiebreaker across Burton schools, measured as a straight-line distance from home to school gate. Last-distance-offered figures from previous years give the clearest indication of realistic catchment radii.

crewe.seoTitle: Schools in Crewe Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
crewe.seoDescription: Crewe catchment area schools: 44 schools across Crewe and surrounding Cheshire East villages. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Crewe's 44 schools are administered by Cheshire East Council and cover the town's distinct neighbourhoods - Wistaston, Shavington, Haslington and Nantwich - each with their own primary feeder clusters. The town grew around its railway works and the school estate reflects a mix of Victorian-era and post-war builds, many since converted to academy status.

Cheshire East publishes its secondary school catchment areas on its website each autumn. For Crewe, Monks Croft and The Ruskin Academy are key secondaries, with oversubscription resolving primarily on proximity to the school gate after looked-after children and sibling preferences.

Several Crewe primaries also offer nursery provision, making them popular first choices for families settling in the town. Applications for Reception places open in September for entry the following September, with the national offer day in April.

grantham.seoTitle: Schools in Grantham Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
grantham.seoDescription: Grantham catchment area: 44 schools across Grantham town and South Kesteven villages. Selective grammar options, catchment maps and 2026 admissions guide.
paragraphs: Grantham sits in South Kesteven district in Lincolnshire and its 44 schools serve both the town and a scatter of fenland and wolds villages nearby. Lincolnshire County Council coordinates all maintained school admissions, publishing catchment boundaries and criteria each autumn.

Selective education is a feature of Grantham's secondary landscape: Kesteven and Grantham Girls' School and The King's School are grammar schools requiring the Lincolnshire selection test. Non-selective secondary places - at Walton Girls' High and Sir William Robertson Academy - are allocated on catchment proximity.

Primary catchments in Grantham are street-level, so a move of a few hundred metres can change which school is nearest. Families should download the most recent published catchment maps from Lincolnshire County Council before submitting a preference.

great-yarmouth.seoTitle: Schools in Great Yarmouth Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
great-yarmouth.seoDescription: Great Yarmouth area schools: 44 schools across the town and surrounding Norfolk Broads villages. Catchment boundaries, admissions criteria and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Great Yarmouth's 44 schools extend well beyond the seafront town into the surrounding Norfolk Broads communities - Caister-on-Sea, Hemsby, Ormesby, Martham and Ludham all have their own primaries. Norfolk County Council coordinates maintained school admissions and publishes catchment area maps for each school annually.

Great Yarmouth High School and Ormiston Venture Academy are the main secondary options in the town itself, both operating under academy arrangements with their own individual admissions policies. Families should check each school's prospectus carefully as criteria can differ from the Norfolk default.

Village primary catchments in the Broads area are tightly drawn around each settlement. Parents in outlying areas between two villages should verify their exact catchment before assuming their nearest-looking school is actually their designated one.

crawley.seoTitle: Schools in Crawley Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
crawley.seoDescription: Crawley catchment area: 44 schools across West Sussex new town neighbourhoods including Three Bridges, Pound Hill, Ifield and Maidenbower. 2026 admissions guide.
paragraphs: Crawley is a planned new town and its 44 schools map closely onto its distinct residential neighbourhoods - Three Bridges, Pound Hill, Maidenbower, Ifield, Langley Green and Broadfield each have their own primary feeder schools. West Sussex County Council coordinates maintained school admissions, publishing catchment boundaries and criteria each October.

Secondary school provision in Crawley includes Hazelwick, Oriel High, Thomas Bennett Community College and Ifield Community College. All are heavily oversubscribed in typical years; last-distance-offered for out-of-catchment applicants can be very short, so living in or near the defined catchment matters enormously.

Crawley's closeness to Gatwick and the M23 makes it attractive to commuter families, keeping sustained pressure on school places. Families who move into the area mid-year should contact West Sussex admissions promptly as in-year places are limited.

horsham.seoTitle: Schools in Horsham Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
horsham.seoDescription: Horsham catchment area: 44 schools across the market town and surrounding West Sussex villages. Catchment maps, 2026 admissions criteria and school guide.
paragraphs: Horsham is a prosperous West Sussex market town, and its 44 schools span the town centre as well as surrounding villages such as Billingshurst, Southwater, Henfield and Steyning. West Sussex County Council coordinates admissions and publishes individual school catchment maps each autumn.

The town's secondary schools - Millais, Forest, Tanbridge House, Bohunt Horsham and Farlington - each draw from defined geographic catchment areas. Competition for places is strong; families on the edge of a catchment boundary may fall outside it despite living close to the school, so verifying the exact boundary is essential.

Primary schools in the Horsham district include many Church of England voluntary-aided schools, which apply faith criteria ahead of distance. Non-faith applicants should be aware that a school's proximity to their home does not guarantee a place if the school prioritises faith applicants.

newbury.seoTitle: Schools in Newbury Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
newbury.seoDescription: Newbury catchment area: 43 schools across the West Berkshire market town and Thames Valley villages. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Newbury's 43 schools serve the town itself and a ring of North Wessex Downs villages - Thatcham, Hungerford, Lambourn, Kintbury and the Ilsleys. West Berkshire Council coordinates maintained school admissions, publishing catchment boundaries and oversubscription criteria each autumn.

Secondary provision in Newbury runs through Park House School, St Bartholomew's School and Trinity School, all with defined catchment areas. West Berkshire is not a selective authority, so all secondary places resolve on distance and sibling priority after looked-after children.

Newbury's rural catchment areas can be large: village primaries often draw from several surrounding hamlets, and the last-admitted pupil distance at town primaries reflects genuine competition from the surrounding population. Checking West Berkshire's published distance data from previous years is the most reliable guide.

gillingham.seoTitle: Schools in Gillingham Dorset Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
gillingham.seoDescription: Gillingham (Dorset) catchment area: 43 schools across the north Dorset market town and surrounding villages. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 guide.
paragraphs: Gillingham is a small market town in the Blackmore Vale, and its 43 schools cover a broad rural area across north Dorset - taking in Shaftesbury, Mere, Sturminster Newton, Stalbridge and the surrounding villages. Dorset Council coordinates all maintained school admissions in this area and publishes catchment boundary maps annually.

Gillingham School is the main secondary for the town, drawing from a large rural catchment. Oversubscription resolves on distance; families in the outer villages should check whether their address falls within the defined catchment or would be treated as an out-of-catchment application.

Many primaries in this part of Dorset are small village schools with single or mixed-age classes. Capacity is limited and catchments are drawn tightly around each village, so families in rural hamlets between two settlements should confirm which school their postcode designates them for.

newark.seoTitle: Schools in Newark Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
newark.seoDescription: Newark catchment area: 43 schools across Newark-on-Trent and surrounding Nottinghamshire villages. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Newark-on-Trent's 43 schools serve the historic Nottinghamshire market town and a spread of Trent Valley villages - Southwell, Balderton, Collingham, East Markham and many smaller parishes. Nottinghamshire County Council coordinates all maintained school admissions, publishing catchment maps and oversubscription criteria each autumn.

Secondary school provision in Newark runs through the Magnus Academy, the Minster School, Lilac Grove Academy and Dukeries Academy. All operate individual admissions policies; families should check each school's specific criteria as they differ from each other and from the Nottinghamshire default.

Village primaries around Newark are typically small and heavily oversubscribed by local residents, leaving little space for out-of-catchment applicants. Using the school's published last-offered distance from prior years will give the most reliable sense of whether an address realistically qualifies.

dagenham.seoTitle: Schools in Dagenham Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
dagenham.seoDescription: Dagenham catchment area: 42 schools across the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham. Admissions criteria, catchment boundaries and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Dagenham forms the eastern half of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham and its 42 schools reflect the borough's dense residential character - primarily primary schools serving each housing estate, from Becontree in the west to Marks Gate in the east. The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham acts as the admissions authority for community schools and coordinates pan-London secondary applications.

Primary school catchments in Dagenham are small: with many schools sitting close together across the Becontree estate, the last-admitted distance at popular schools can be as little as a few hundred metres. Siblings and looked-after children take precedence, then straightforward home-to-school distance.

Secondary school choices open up beyond Dagenham itself through the pan-London application process, but schools in the immediate area include Robert Clack School (outstanding), Jo Richardson Community School and Sydney Russell. Application data from the borough shows most secondary pupils attend schools within or immediately adjacent to Dagenham.

harlow.seoTitle: Schools in Harlow Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
harlow.seoDescription: Harlow catchment area: 42 schools across Essex new town neighbourhoods and surrounding villages. Catchment maps, admissions criteria and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Harlow is a post-war Essex new town whose 42 schools are spread across its residential neighbourhoods - Staple Tye, Netteswell, Latton, Church Langley, Potter Street and the older town-centre wards. Essex County Council coordinates maintained school admissions and publishes neighbourhood catchment boundaries each autumn.

Harlow's new-town design means each residential neighbourhood was planned with a primary school: many primaries are Church of England voluntary-aided schools built alongside housing estates, and faith criteria apply ahead of distance for practising Christian families. For non-faith applicants, straightforward proximity determines priority.

Secondary options in Harlow include Passmores Academy, Stewards Academy and Burnt Mill Academy. Essex's published admissions data shows last-offered distances that vary significantly between schools year on year, reflecting population movements across the borough.

woking.seoTitle: Schools in Woking Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
woking.seoDescription: Woking catchment area: 42 schools across the Surrey commuter town and surrounding villages. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Woking is one of Surrey's main commuter towns and its 42 schools serve a mix of urban neighbourhoods - Horsell, Knaphill, Sheerwater, Pyrford and Old Woking - plus rural parishes stretching to Send, Ripley and Bisley. Surrey County Council coordinates maintained school admissions and publishes catchment maps annually.

Secondary school places in Woking are hotly contested: Winston Churchill School, Woking High School and Bishop David Brown School all have defined catchment areas, and the last-admitted distance in popular years has been as low as 0.5 miles for in-catchment applicants. Living within the published catchment is close to essential at the most popular schools.

Surrey's admissions system uses a straight-line measurement from the home address to the school entrance. Families who have recently moved should ensure their new address is registered with Surrey County Council's admissions team before the October secondary closing date.

northwich.seoTitle: Schools in Northwich Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
northwich.seoDescription: Northwich catchment area: 41 schools across the Cheshire West market town and Weaver Valley villages. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Northwich sits in the Weaver Valley at the heart of Cheshire West and Chester, and its 41 schools span the town itself and surrounding villages including Winsford, Middlewich, Moulton, Hartford and Weaverham. Cheshire West and Chester Council coordinates all maintained school admissions, publishing catchment boundaries each autumn.

Secondary provision in Northwich runs through Hartford High School, Rudheath Academy and The Weaverham School, each with defined geographic catchments. Cheshire West operates a mixed secondary landscape with no selective schools in this area, so all places resolve on distance after looked-after children and siblings.

The salt-mining heritage of the Northwich area has left some areas of ground subsidence that have historically affected school building footprints; most schools are now on stable modern sites. School places are moderately competitive, with last-admitted distances typically in the 0.5-2 mile range depending on the school and year.

lancaster.seoTitle: Schools in Lancaster Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
lancaster.seoDescription: Lancaster catchment area: 41 schools across the Lancashire city and Morecambe Bay villages. Catchment maps, admissions criteria and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Lancaster is Lancashire's county town and a university city, and its 41 schools serve the city itself plus the Morecambe Bay coastline communities of Morecambe, Heysham and the Lune Valley villages. Lancashire County Council coordinates maintained school admissions across the area and publishes catchment maps annually.

Secondary schools in Lancaster include Lancaster Girls' Grammar School (selective), with the eleven-plus test administered by Lancashire each September. Non-selective secondaries - Ripley St Thomas, Central Lancaster High and Morecambe Bay Academy - operate defined catchment areas, with proximity as the main tiebreaker.

Lancaster's university population creates a degree of transience in the primary school estate, so place availability can vary year on year. Families should apply in the autumn before their desired September entry and confirm catchment boundaries directly with Lancashire admissions, as minor updates are published annually.

chichester.seoTitle: Schools in Chichester Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
chichester.seoDescription: Chichester catchment area: 41 schools across the West Sussex cathedral city and South Downs villages. Catchment maps, admissions criteria and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Chichester is West Sussex's cathedral city, and its 41 schools cover the city and a wide arc of South Downs and coastal villages - Bosham, Emsworth, Selsey, East Wittering, Midhurst and Petworth. West Sussex County Council coordinates maintained school admissions and publishes individual school catchment maps each October.

Secondary schools in Chichester include Chichester High School, Bishop Luffa Church of England School (faith criteria apply) and Ormiston Chichester Academy. Bishop Luffa's faith admissions criteria mean regular church attendance must be evidenced; for non-faith applicants, distance is the decisive factor.

Rural primaries across the Chichester Plain and South Downs AONB are typically small and popular with local families. Last-offered distances at the most popular city primaries can be very short, reflecting demand from the historic city's residential areas and from families who have relocated from London.

keighley.seoTitle: Schools in Keighley Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
keighley.seoDescription: Keighley catchment area: 40 schools across Bradford's Aire Valley town and Brontë Country moorland villages. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 guide.
paragraphs: Keighley sits in the Aire Valley in the Bradford local authority district, and its 40 schools span a varied geography - the town centre and Ingrow to the south, Silsden and Steeton to the north, and moorland villages such as Haworth, Oxenhope and Stanbury to the west. Bradford Council coordinates admissions for maintained schools and publishes catchment boundary maps annually.

Keighley and the surrounding Worth Valley are strongly associated with the Brontë sisters, drawing families to the village primaries of Haworth and Stanbury. These small schools are popular but have limited capacity; catchment boundaries are tightly drawn and last-offered distances can be very short.

Secondary schools in Keighley include Dixons Kings Academy, Holy Family Catholic School and Greenhead College (sixth form only). Bradford has a legacy of faith-school provision across both primary and secondary phases; families should check each school's admissions criteria carefully, as CofE and Catholic schools apply faith criteria ahead of distance.

gravesend.seoTitle: Schools in Gravesend Catchment Area 2026 - Map & Admissions Guide
gravesend.seoDescription: Gravesend catchment area: 40 schools across the Kent Thames estuary town and Northfleet area. Admissions criteria, catchment maps and 2026 school guide.
paragraphs: Gravesend and neighbouring Northfleet sit on the south bank of the Thames estuary in north-west Kent, and their 40 schools serve a densely settled urban corridor stretching from Cobham and Meopham in the rural south to the river frontage in the north. Kent County Council coordinates maintained school admissions and publishes catchment boundary maps annually.

Kent operates one of England's few remaining fully selective secondary systems: pupils sit the Kent Test at the start of Year 6, and a pass is required to apply to grammar schools such as Gravesend Grammar School for Boys or Mayfield Grammar School for girls. Non-selective secondary places at Northfleet Technology College and St John's Catholic Comprehensive resolve on distance after looked-after children and siblings.

Primary schools in Gravesend are served by a mix of community and Church of England schools. In-catchment places at community primaries resolve on distance, while CofE schools apply faith criteria first. Gravesend's housing growth means some schools operate close to or above published capacity, making early engagement with Kent admissions important.

wisbech.seoTitle: Wisbech School Catchment Areas 2026 - 39 Schools by Postcode
wisbech.seoDescription: Wisbech area catchment finder: 26 primary + 3 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Cambridgeshire, Lincolnshire and Norfolk admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Wisbech has 39 schools spread across a boundary zone where Cambridgeshire, Lincolnshire and Norfolk meet. Because the town sits at the edge of three local authority areas, which council coordinates admissions depends on exactly which side of the boundary your address falls. Most Wisbech town schools are administered by Cambridgeshire County Council, but families in villages to the north and east may fall under Norfolk or Lincolnshire.

Cambridgeshire uses a combination of sibling priority and straight-line distance as tiebreakers for community schools. Wisbech Grammar School is a selective independent school, while secondary admissions in the state sector are coordinated by the county. The Cambridgeshire admissions round deadline is typically in mid-January for September entry, with a separate Hampshire-style rural supplementary form for faith schools.

macclesfield.seoTitle: Macclesfield School Catchment Areas 2026 - 39 Schools by Postcode
macclesfield.seoDescription: Macclesfield area catchment finder: 29 primary + 4 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Cheshire East 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Macclesfield has 39 schools, with 29 primaries and 4 secondary schools administered primarily by Cheshire East Council. The town includes a range of community schools, Church of England primaries and one Catholic secondary (St John Fisher). Cheshire East uses straight-line distance as the main tiebreaker after looked-after children and siblings - popular primaries in the town centre and Tytherington areas can be competitive.

Secondary admissions in Macclesfield are non-selective; Macclesfield Academy, The Fallibroome Academy and Tytherington School each draw from across the town. Families on the Staffordshire border should check whether their address falls under Cheshire East or Staffordshire Moorlands, as the boundary affects both the secondary school and the coordinating authority for the admissions round.

bishop-auckland.seoTitle: Bishop Auckland School Catchment Areas 2026 - 39 Schools by Postcode
bishop-auckland.seoDescription: Bishop Auckland area catchment finder: 30 primary + 4 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. County Durham 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bishop Auckland has 39 schools, including 30 primaries and 4 secondaries, all coordinated by Durham County Council. County Durham operates a designated catchment area system for most community schools - your home address determines your catchment school, and places are offered to catchment pupils before out-of-catchment applicants. Bishop Auckland's catchment boundaries cover several distinct communities including Spennymoor, Shildon, and the surrounding Wear Valley villages.

Secondary schools in the Bishop Auckland area include King James I Academy and Durham Johnston (selective sixth form). County Durham's admissions round opens in September for secondary places starting the following September, with the national deadline in October. Families moving into the area should contact Durham County Council's School Admissions team promptly, as catchment schools can be full and in-year transfers to popular schools are not guaranteed.

andover.seoTitle: Andover School Catchment Areas 2026 - 39 Schools by Postcode
andover.seoDescription: Andover area catchment finder: 28 primary + 3 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Hampshire and Wiltshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Andover has 39 schools, with most of the town's 28 primaries and 3 secondary schools administered by Hampshire County Council. Villages around Andover, particularly to the south and west, may fall under Wiltshire Council. Hampshire uses a designated school system where each home address has an associated nearest school, and priority is given to catchment pupils at community schools - this makes address verification essential when applying.

Hampshire's secondary schools in Andover include John Hanson Community School and Winton Community Academy. Hampshire operates a grammar school system in certain parts of the county, but Andover itself is in the non-selective zone. The Hampshire coordinated admissions round deadline is in mid-October for secondary places, significantly earlier than the national deadline of October 31.

wellingborough.seoTitle: Wellingborough School Catchment Areas 2026 - 39 Schools by Postcode
wellingborough.seoDescription: Wellingborough area catchment finder: 29 primary + 5 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. North Northamptonshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Wellingborough has 39 schools, including 29 primaries and 5 secondaries, all administered by North Northamptonshire Council - one of the two unitary authorities created in 2021 when Northamptonshire County Council was abolished. North Northamptonshire uses straight-line distance as the main tiebreaker for community schools, and several Wellingborough primaries in the town centre and Redwell areas have been consistently oversubscribed.

Secondary admissions in Wellingborough are non-selective. Wrenn School, Weavers Academy and Friars School are the main comprehensives serving the town. North Northamptonshire's admissions round follows national deadlines. Families considering Northampton grammar schools should note these are administered by West Northamptonshire Council and require a separate 11-plus registration.

bromley.seoTitle: Bromley School Catchment Areas 2026 - 38 Schools by Postcode
bromley.seoDescription: Bromley area catchment finder: 22 primary + 7 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. London Borough of Bromley 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bromley has 38 schools in the pages covering the Bromley postcode area, with most administered by the London Borough of Bromley. The borough is notable for retaining selective grammar schools - Newstead Wood School for Girls, St Olave's and St Peter's Grammar School, and Bromley's single boys' grammar, are among the most sought-after secondaries in south-east London. Families must register separately for the Bromley 11-plus test, which runs in September ahead of the main admissions round.

For non-selective secondary admissions, Bromley Council uses straight-line distance as the main tiebreaker. Addresses near the Lewisham or Croydon border should confirm the administering borough for their target school. Popular primaries in areas such as Chislehurst, Shortlands and Petts Wood have been historically oversubscribed; checking the published last-distance-offered data from previous years gives the most realistic guide to catchment proximity.

dudley.seoTitle: Dudley School Catchment Areas 2026 - 38 Schools by Postcode
dudley.seoDescription: Dudley area catchment finder: 23 primary + 8 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Dudley Metropolitan Borough 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Dudley has 38 schools covering the town and surrounding communities in the Black Country, with the majority administered by Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council. Dudley uses a catchment area model for most of its community primary schools, meaning each address has a designated catchment school. Secondary admissions are non-selective across the borough, with Dudley's eight secondary schools including academies and faith schools drawing from across the town.

Dudley's school landscape includes a significant number of academy schools, some of which set their own admissions policies. Families applying to academy schools in Dudley should read each school's individual admissions policy, as oversubscription criteria can differ from the council's standard scheme. Schools near the Staffordshire border or the Sandwell boundary may be administered by those authorities - address postcodes near DY3, DY5 and DY6 should be checked carefully.

truro.seoTitle: Truro School Catchment Areas 2026 - 38 Schools by Postcode
truro.seoDescription: Truro area catchment finder: 26 primary + 3 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Cornwall Council 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Truro has 38 schools, including 26 primaries and 3 secondary schools, all administered by Cornwall Council. As Cornwall's county town and administrative capital, Truro sits at the centre of a wide catchment zone for secondary education, drawing pupils from villages across the Fal valley, Roseland peninsula and Carnon Downs. Cornwall Council uses the community school system with a designated area model - primary catchment boundaries are drawn around village and neighbourhood schools.

Truro's secondaries include Truro Learning Academy and Richard Lander School, both non-selective comprehensives. Truro School is a selective fee-paying school with its own admissions process. Cornwall's large rural geography means some families face significant travel distances; the council operates Home to School Transport eligibility based on designated school distance thresholds. The national admissions round deadlines apply in Cornwall.

conwy.seoTitle: Conwy School Catchment Areas 2026 - 38 Schools by Postcode
conwy.seoDescription: Conwy area catchment finder: 38 schools mapped to your postcode. Conwy County Borough Council 2026 Welsh admissions criteria, Ofsted/Estyn ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Conwy has 38 schools administered by Conwy County Borough Council in north Wales. The borough covers a wide geographic area including coastal towns such as Llandudno, Conwy town, Colwyn Bay and Abergele, as well as inland communities in the Conwy Valley. Welsh medium education is a significant factor in school choice here - a number of primary schools in the county teach primarily or exclusively through Welsh, and families must specify their language medium preference when applying.

Conwy County Borough Council coordinates admissions for all maintained schools under the Welsh national admissions framework, with application deadlines aligned to the Welsh Government's admissions timetable (typically November for primary and December for secondary). Estyn, rather than Ofsted, inspects Welsh schools. Families moving to Conwy from England should note that the Welsh admissions round has slightly different timelines and that many Welsh-medium schools have their own language assessments.

richmond.seoTitle: Richmond School Catchment Areas 2026 - 37 Schools by Postcode
richmond.seoDescription: Richmond area catchment finder: 22 primary + 4 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Richmond upon Thames 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Richmond has 37 schools, with most administered by the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames - one of London's highest-demand boroughs for school places. Richmond upon Thames uses straight-line distance as the primary tiebreaker for community schools after looked-after children and siblings. Popular primaries in areas such as East Sheen, Kew, and Ham have been significantly oversubscribed in recent years, with some schools offering places to children living less than half a mile away.

Secondary admissions in Richmond upon Thames are highly competitive. Grey Court School, Waldegrave School, and Richmond Park Academy each attract strong demand. The borough has no selective grammar schools; all state secondaries are comprehensive. Families in Richmond should also note that the Kingston upon Thames borough boundary runs through parts of the area, so some addresses that feel like 'Richmond' may apply through a different council.

maidenhead.seoTitle: Maidenhead School Catchment Areas 2026 - 37 Schools by Postcode
maidenhead.seoDescription: Maidenhead area catchment finder: 24 primary + 5 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Windsor and Maidenhead 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Maidenhead has 37 schools administered primarily by the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead (RBWM), with some village schools to the north under Buckinghamshire Council. RBWM uses a proximity-based model for community schools, with straight-line distance as the main tiebreaker. Maidenhead's proximity to the M4 corridor makes it a desirable commuter town, and several primaries in the Cookham, Furze Platt and Cox Green areas have been consistently oversubscribed.

Berkshire retains grammar schools, and families in Maidenhead have access to the selective 11-plus system. Grammar schools in Maidenhead itself include Desborough College (boys) and Newlands Girls School. Registration for the Berkshire 11-plus must be completed by June, significantly before the main admissions round. Non-selective secondary admissions in RBWM use straight-line distance tiebreakers aligned with national deadlines.

runcorn.seoTitle: Runcorn School Catchment Areas 2026 - 37 Schools by Postcode
runcorn.seoDescription: Runcorn area catchment finder: 29 primary + 4 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Halton Borough Council 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Runcorn has 37 schools, including 29 primaries and 4 secondary schools, administered by Halton Borough Council - the unitary authority covering Runcorn and Widnes. Halton uses a designated catchment area system for most community primary schools, with straight-line distance as the tiebreaker when catchment places are oversubscribed. Runcorn's planned new-town layout means catchment boundaries broadly follow the distinct 'villages' or residential areas built during the 1960s and 1970s expansion.

Runcorn's four secondary schools serve the whole town. Halton coordinates secondary admissions with the national October deadline. Some secondary schools in Runcorn have sixth forms; families considering post-16 options should check individual school provision. Addresses near the Cheshire West and Chester boundary, particularly in the Preston Brook and Murdishaw areas, should verify which authority coordinates admissions for their nearest school.

tunbridge-wells.seoTitle: Tunbridge Wells School Catchment Areas 2026 - 37 Schools by Postcode
tunbridge-wells.seoDescription: Tunbridge Wells area catchment finder: 23 primary + 6 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Kent and East Sussex 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Tunbridge Wells has 37 schools, with the majority in Kent administered by Kent County Council, and some on the southern and eastern edges under East Sussex County Council. Kent is a selective county, and Tunbridge Wells is home to grammar schools including Tunbridge Wells Grammar School for Boys and Tunbridge Wells Girls' Grammar School. Families must register for the Kent 11-plus (KS2 SEMH) by June in Year 5, with the test sitting in September of Year 6.

For primary admissions, Kent County Council uses a combination of sibling priority and distance for community schools. Tunbridge Wells has several Church of England and Catholic primaries with additional faith criteria. Families near the East Sussex border should check whether their address falls in East Sussex - the county uses a non-selective system, so the choice of secondary school type available depends on which side of the border you live.

stroud.seoTitle: Stroud School Catchment Areas 2026 - 37 Schools by Postcode
stroud.seoDescription: Stroud area catchment finder: 26 primary + 4 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Gloucestershire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Stroud has 37 schools, including 26 primaries and 4 secondary schools, coordinated by Gloucestershire County Council. Stroud sits in a steep-sided valley in the Cotswold fringe, and the geography directly affects school catchment areas - communities in Nailsworth, Painswick, Minchinhampton and Stonehouse each have distinct village school traditions. Gloucestershire County Council uses a designated area model for community primaries, with families assigned to their nearest appropriate school.

Secondary admissions in the Stroud area are non-selective. Marling School (boys' grammar) in Stroud is one of Gloucestershire's selective grammar schools - registration for the 11-plus must be completed early in Year 6. Stroud High School is an independent selective girls' school. For comprehensive secondary admissions, Gloucestershire uses straight-line distance tiebreakers and the national October deadline.

Worcestershire County Council uses straight-line distance as the primary tiebreaker for community schools after looked-after children and siblings.

Secondary admissions in Redditch are non-selective; Worcestershire does not operate grammar schools in this area. The relatively high number of secondary schools for the town's population means year-group sizes are spread across more schools. Families should check the published admission numbers for each school carefully. Redditch borders the West Midlands conurbation, and some families living near the boundary with Bromsgrove or Solihull may have access to schools in those districts as well.

tonbridge.seoTitle: Tonbridge School Catchment Areas 2026 - 37 Schools by Postcode

paragraphs: Tonbridge has 37 schools, with 22 primaries and 7 secondary schools all administered by Kent County Council. Kent is a selective county, and Tonbridge has a strong grammar school tradition - Tonbridge Grammar School (girls) and the fee-paying Tonbridge School (boys, independent) are the most prominent selective schools in the town. For state grammar entry, families must register for the Kent 11-plus test by June in Year 5.

For community primary admissions, Kent County Council uses a combination of sibling priority and straight-line distance. Several Church of England primaries and Catholic primaries in Tonbridge have additional faith criteria. Secondary non-selective options include several comprehensives and academies; families whose children do not pass or sit the 11-plus should verify the admissions policy and distance thresholds for each non-selective secondary, as popular schools in Tonbridge can be oversubscribed.

wokingham.seoTitle: Wokingham School Catchment Areas 2026 - 36 Schools by Postcode

paragraphs: Wokingham has 36 schools administered across two local authorities: most town schools are under Wokingham Borough Council, while some schools in the Finchampstead and Sandhurst areas may fall under Bracknell Forest Borough Council. Berkshire retains grammar schools, and Wokingham Borough operates both selective and non-selective secondary schools - families must register for the Berkshire 11-plus by June in Year 5 if considering grammar school entry.

For community primary admissions, Wokingham Borough uses straight-line distance as the main tiebreaker. The borough has seen significant housing growth in areas such as Arborfield and Shinfield, with new schools opening to serve new developments. Families in newer housing estates should check which school's catchment area applies to their specific address, as admissions policies for recently-built schools can differ from neighbouring long-established schools.

huntingdon.seoTitle: Huntingdon School Catchment Areas 2026 - 36 Schools by Postcode

For primary admissions, Cambridgeshire uses a combination of sibling priority and straight-line distance for community schools, with additional faith criteria for Church of England schools. Villages around Huntingdon - including Brampton, Godmanchester and Hemingford - each have their own primary schools with distinct catchment areas. Families in the Bedford and North Cambridgeshire border zone should verify which authority coordinates admissions for their nearest school, as the boundary between Cambridgeshire and Bedford Borough runs through this area.

For primary admissions, Kent County Council uses sibling priority and straight-line distance for community schools. Sevenoaks district is one of the most affluent in the South East, with several Church of England village primaries adding faith criteria. Non-selective secondary options in the area include Knole Academy. Families in villages towards the Tonbridge or Maidstone borders should check which secondary school's admissions zone covers their address.

The Deanes operates a designated catchment zone, while King John and The Appleton use proximity after sibling and looked-after children priorities. Castle Point and Rochford are the combined admissions authority area, so applying to schools just across the district boundary requires checking each school's individual policy on the Essex admissions portal.

Chase Terrace Academy draws from a wide residential area across the town, while Erasmus Darwin Academy admits on proximity after specialist criteria. camberley.seoTitle: Camberley School Catchment Areas 2026 - 18 Primary & 3 Secondary | Surrey Heath
camberley.seoDescription: Camberley catchment finder: 25 Surrey schools - 18 primary + 3 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.

Collingwood College is a large non-selective comprehensive admitting around 300 pupils per year, while Tomlinscote is a similar-sized school in the southern part of the town. Kings International College operates an all-through model from Years 7 to 13. Secondary applications in Surrey are submitted through the online portal each October, with National Offer Day in March.

grays.seoTitle: Grays School Catchment Areas 2026 - 16 Primary & 7 Secondary | Thurrock

Grays Convent High School allocates places on faith criteria first, drawing Catholic pupils from across Thurrock. Both secondary schools are academy-run and admit on standard comprehensive criteria, with proximity the key tiebreaker after sibling priority. Mulberry Academy serves much of the central and western residential areas, while Ark Alexandra is positioned to the east of the town centre. East Sussex secondary applications close in October, with offers made on 1 March National Offer Day.

Saffron Walden County High School is a large converter academy drawing from a wide rural catchment that includes villages across Uttlesford district; the school's published last-distance-offered figure is worth checking before applying from outlying villages. Joyce Frankland Academy in nearby Newport offers an alternative secondary option for families in the north of the catchment area. Essex secondary applications are made online through the county portal each October.

Primary applications to Brent schools close on 15 January.

kendal.seoTitle: Kendal School Catchment Areas 2026 - 16 Primary & 2 Secondary | Westmorland and Furness
kendal.seoDescription: Kendal catchment finder: 24 schools - 16 primary + 2 secondary catchments mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and last distance offered - free.

Both are converter academies with their own admissions policies, though oversubscription criteria broadly follow the LA model. Rural village primaries in the Kendal area sometimes have spare capacity year-on-year, making them a practical alternative to oversubscribed town-centre schools.

Its oversubscription criteria prioritise looked-after children and siblings, then proximity by straight-line distance - with competition typically most acute for addresses in the town centre and established residential streets. Cheshire East secondary applications open in September and close in late October.

basildon.seoDescription: All 35 schools in Basildon including 29 primaries and 5 secondaries. Catchment boundaries and admissions policies for Essex 2026.

Essex County Council co-ordinates admissions for maintained schools, while academy trusts in Basildon handle their own processes. Five schools serve Church of England and Catholic communities. With five secondary schools covering a significant population, catchment boundaries are tightly contested - Essex publishes secondary school offer distances each spring to help families plan ahead.

caerphilly.seoTitle: Caerphilly School Catchment Areas 2026 - Welsh & English Medium Schools

Parents should apply early and verify whether their address falls within the Welsh-medium or English-medium catchment, as the zones do not always align with parish or ward boundaries.

Weston's five secondaries serve a mix of urban and rural feeder primary schools. scarborough.seoTitle: Scarborough School Catchment Areas 2026 - North Yorkshire Schools Guide
scarborough.seoDescription: All 34 schools in Scarborough including 21 primaries and 5 secondaries. Catchment boundaries and admissions policies for North Yorkshire 2026.

hitchin.seoTitle: Hitchin School Catchment Areas 2026 - Central Bedfordshire Schools
