dover.seoTitle: Dover School Catchment Areas 2026 - Kent Schools Map
dover.seoDescription: All 33 schools in Dover including 22 primaries and 6 secondaries. Catchment boundaries and admissions policies for Kent 2026.
paragraphs: Dover and its surrounding villages in Kent have 33 schools - 22 primaries and six secondaries. Eleven schools carry a faith designation and 13 operate as academies. Kent is one of the last counties to retain a selective grammar school system, and Dover's six secondaries include both grammar schools for those who pass the 11-plus and non-selective academies.

Kent County Council co-ordinates admissions for the area, with the 11-plus test administered each September for Year 7 entry. Families in border villages such as Eythorne, Lydden, and River should confirm whether their address qualifies for Dover's secondaries or falls within the Canterbury or Folkestone preference zones. Kent publishes secondary allocation outcomes and last-distance figures annually.

rhondda-cynon-taff.seoTitle: Rhondda Cynon Taf School Catchment Areas 2026 - Welsh Schools Guide
rhondda-cynon-taff.seoDescription: All 33 schools in Rhondda Cynon Taf including Welsh-medium and English-medium provision across the valleys. Catchment boundaries and admissions for 2026.
paragraphs: Rhondda Cynon Taf County Borough Council administers school admissions across the three valleys - Rhondda Fawr, Rhondda Fach, and the Cynon Valley. The borough's 33 schools include both Welsh-medium and English-medium provision, with Welsh-medium demand particularly strong in the Llantrisant and Pontyclun commuter belt.

Families should be aware that Welsh-medium and English-medium schools in Rhondda Cynon Taf operate separate oversubscription criteria and catchment zones. The council publishes its annual admissions guide each September, and parents selecting Welsh-medium education are advised to confirm language of instruction preferences early, as some schools offer transitional bilingual classes rather than fully Welsh-medium provision.

stourbridge.seoTitle: Stourbridge School Catchment Areas 2026 - Dudley Schools Guide
stourbridge.seoDescription: All 32 schools in Stourbridge including 21 primaries and 7 secondaries. Catchment boundaries and admissions policies for Dudley 2026.
paragraphs: Stourbridge, in the Dudley metropolitan borough of the West Midlands, has 32 schools - 21 primaries and seven secondaries, with 17 academies and seven faith-designated settings. As the most affluent part of the Black Country, Stourbridge's schools have seen sustained demand, and some secondaries have historically appeared in regional league tables for GCSE performance.

Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council co-ordinates school admissions using a catchment-and-distance model. Families in the Pedmore, Hagley, and Hagley Road corridors bordering Bromsgrove and Wyre Forest should verify which council's scheme applies to their address. Stourbridge's seven secondaries draw from a mix of prosperous suburban and semi-rural feeder primaries, and 'last distance offered' figures are published by Dudley Council each April.

widnes.seoTitle: Widnes School Catchment Areas 2026 - Cheshire & Knowsley Schools
widnes.seoDescription: All 32 schools in Widnes including 20 primaries and 3 secondaries. Catchment boundaries and admissions policies for 2026.
paragraphs: Widnes and its surrounding area straddle the Cheshire West and Knowsley council boundary. The town has 32 schools - 20 primaries and three secondaries - with 14 faith-designated settings, the highest proportion of any area in this grouping, reflecting Widnes's strong Catholic community heritage linked to Irish immigration in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

Admissions in Widnes can be administered by either Knowsley, Cheshire West, or Halton Council depending on the school's location and governance. Eight schools operate as academies with independent admissions. Parents should check the specific admissions authority for each school, as a Catholic primary and a community primary on the same street may use entirely different oversubscription criteria and application portals.

southport.seoTitle: Southport School Catchment Areas 2026 - Sefton Schools Guide
southport.seoDescription: All 32 schools in Southport including 21 primaries and 5 secondaries. Catchment boundaries and admissions policies for Sefton 2026.
paragraphs: Southport in Sefton, Merseyside has 32 schools - 21 primaries and five secondaries, with 12 academies and 11 faith-designated schools. The resort town has a strong independent and Catholic school tradition, and competition for places at certain faith secondaries can be intense, particularly for families who are not parishioners of the associated church.

Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council co-ordinates school admissions for the area. The five secondary schools in Southport serve both the town and the outlying villages of Churchtown and Ainsdale. Families applying to faith schools must submit supplementary information forms (SIFs) directly to the school in addition to the council application - missing the SIF deadline is a common and costly error in Sefton's admissions cycle.

waterlooville.seoTitle: Waterlooville School Catchment Areas 2026 - Hampshire Schools Map
waterlooville.seoDescription: All 32 schools in Waterlooville including 22 primaries and 5 secondaries. Catchment boundaries and admissions policies for Hampshire 2026.
paragraphs: Waterlooville and its surrounding villages in South-East Hampshire have 32 schools - 22 primaries and five secondaries. Unlike many comparable Hampshire towns, only three of these schools operate as academies, meaning Hampshire County Council coordinates the vast majority of admissions using its published scheme. Four schools carry faith designations - three Church of England and one Catholic.

Hampshire administers one of the largest school admissions systems in England, and Waterlooville's position between Portsmouth, Havant, and the South Downs National Park means families in outlying villages such as Hambledon, Denmead, and Clanfield may have more limited secondary options than those in the town centre. Hampshire publishes secondary school offer distances each March to help families assess their realistic chances at each school.

morpeth.seoTitle: Morpeth School Catchment Areas 2026 - Northumberland Schools Guide
morpeth.seoDescription: All 32 schools in Morpeth including 24 primaries and 2 secondaries. Catchment boundaries and admissions policies for Northumberland 2026.
paragraphs: Morpeth and the surrounding communities of southern Northumberland have 32 schools - 24 primaries and two secondaries. Twelve schools operate as academies, and 11 carry faith designations reflecting the area's Church of England village school tradition. The two secondary schools serve a large rural catchment extending from Ashington coalfield villages in the east to the Northumberland uplands in the west.

Northumberland County Council co-ordinates admissions for maintained schools in the area. With only two secondary schools serving such a wide geographic area, demand can be significant for families closer to Morpeth town, while rural families in villages such as Amble, Broomhill, and Ellington may qualify for transport assistance to their allocated school. Northumberland publishes its secondary allocation outcomes each spring.

uxbridge.seoTitle: Uxbridge School Catchment Areas 2026 - 31 Schools, Postcode Checker
uxbridge.seoDescription: Uxbridge catchment finder: 15 primary + 7 secondary schools in Hillingdon, every boundary mapped to your postcode. Ofsted ratings, admissions criteria and distances offered last year.
paragraphs: Uxbridge's 31 schools sit within the London Borough of Hillingdon's admissions remit, covering 15 primaries and 7 secondaries alongside 9 specialist and all-through settings. Hillingdon operates a combination of catchment-distance and oversubscription criteria for community schools, with boundaries recalculated each cycle based on the furthest distance offered in the previous round.

Demand for secondary places in Uxbridge is high owing to its position between Ealing, Hillingdon town centre and the Colne Valley - several secondary schools consistently close to applicants living outside their historic catchment footprint. Parents are advised to check the measured walking-route distances used by Hillingdon rather than straight-line estimates when assessing realistic chances.

altrincham.seoTitle: Altrincham School Catchment Areas 2026 - 31 Schools, Postcode Checker
altrincham.seoDescription: Altrincham catchment finder: 17 primary + 8 secondary schools in Trafford, every boundary mapped to your postcode. Admissions distances, Ofsted ratings and 2026 criteria.
paragraphs: Altrincham's 31 schools fall under Trafford's coordinated admissions scheme, with 17 primaries and 8 secondaries serving the affluent south-Manchester corridor stretching from Hale and Bowdon through to Timperley. Trafford community schools use measured straight-line distance as the principal oversubscription criterion; the most sought-after primaries - including Navigation and Stamford Park - have historically closed to new applicants within a kilometre of the school gate.

Secondary allocation in Altrincham is shaped significantly by the selective grammar schools in the borough; families who do not sit the Trafford grammar test compete for places at non-selective secondaries where catchment radii can shift markedly year on year. The borough publishes its full offer statistics each spring, and historical distance data is available through catchment.school to help families gauge realistic chances well before application deadlines.

dewsbury.seoTitle: Dewsbury School Catchment Areas 2026 - 31 Schools, Postcode Checker
dewsbury.seoDescription: Dewsbury catchment finder: 19 primary + 4 secondary schools in Kirklees, mapped to your postcode. Ofsted ratings, 2026 admissions criteria and distances offered.
paragraphs: Dewsbury's 31 schools form part of Kirklees Council's coordinated admissions system, with 19 primaries and 4 secondaries serving a post-industrial West Yorkshire town that spans Savile Town, Thornhill and Shaw Cross. Kirklees uses a distance-based oversubscription tie-breaker for community schools, with measurements taken as straight-line distances from the child's home address to the school's main entrance.

Secondary choice in Dewsbury is influenced by the town's proximity to Batley and Heckmondwike, giving families reasonable travel access to secondary schools across a wider Kirklees catchment. Parents of children with siblings already at a school benefit from the sibling priority that Kirklees applies before distance - making early decisions about primary school placement especially consequential for longer-term secondary options.

chippenham.seoTitle: Chippenham Area School Catchment Finder 2026 - 31 Schools by Postcode
chippenham.seoDescription: Chippenham area schools: 25 primaries + 3 secondaries in South Gloucestershire, every catchment boundary mapped. Ofsted data, 2026 admissions criteria and distances.
paragraphs: The Chippenham area encompassing South Gloucestershire contains 31 schools - 25 primaries, 3 secondaries and 3 other settings - administered by South Gloucestershire Council under its coordinated admissions scheme. South Gloucestershire uses a combination of sibling priority and measured straight-line distance to the school for community schools, with published offer statistics updated after each National Offer Day.

Rural spread in this corridor means that several village primaries serve tight, locality-specific catchments, and families in settlements like Marshfield or Luckington should check boundary maps carefully before applying to schools that appear geographically close but sit outside the school's historic offer distance. Sibling links are a significant planning factor for families already in the area, as they carry priority above distance for most community schools.

ormskirk.seoTitle: Ormskirk School Catchment Areas 2026 - 31 Schools, Postcode Checker
ormskirk.seoDescription: Ormskirk catchment finder: 22 primary + 3 secondary schools in Lancashire, every boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions, Ofsted ratings and distance data.
paragraphs: Ormskirk's 31 schools are administered by Lancashire County Council, covering 22 primaries and 3 secondaries in a market town that sits between Skelmersdale and Southport in the West Lancashire district. Lancashire's community schools use straight-line distance as the final oversubscription criterion after looked-after children and siblings; the three secondaries serving the town include Ormskirk School and schools in surrounding villages that draw catchment families from a wide rural hinterland.

Primary catchments around Ormskirk are broadly drawn because of the rural character of much of West Lancashire, but in-town primaries such as Aughton Town Green and Ormskirk Asmall can still reach capacity from their immediate neighbourhood. Families considering a move into the area should pay attention to which side of the Ormskirk bypass a property sits on, as this can affect proximity rankings meaningfully for the most popular schools.

yeovil.seoTitle: Yeovil School Catchment Areas 2026 - 31 Schools, Postcode Checker
yeovil.seoDescription: Yeovil catchment finder: 22 primary + 3 secondary schools in Somerset, every boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distances offered.
paragraphs: Yeovil's 31 schools are overseen by Somerset Council, with 22 primaries and 3 secondaries serving the county's second-largest town alongside nursery and specialist provision. Somerset uses a measured straight-line distance tie-breaker for community schools after sibling and medical/social priority bands; the town's secondaries - including The Westfield Academy, Preston School and Buckler's Mead - each draw from distinct residential zones across a town that has grown significantly through peripheral housing developments.

Primary demand in newer Yeovil neighbourhoods such as Brimsmore and Barwick edges can be acute, as catchment distances to nearest schools are shorter and new housing brings sudden population spikes. Somerset's admissions team publishes final distance thresholds each April, and families should use postcode-level mapping to confirm their nearest school before assuming proximity guarantees a place.

lowestoft.seoTitle: Lowestoft School Catchment Areas 2026 - 31 Schools, Postcode Checker
lowestoft.seoDescription: Lowestoft catchment finder: 20 primary + 4 secondary schools in Suffolk, every boundary mapped to your postcode. Ofsted ratings, 2026 admissions criteria and distances.
paragraphs: Lowestoft's 31 schools are administered by Suffolk County Council, with 20 primaries and 4 secondaries serving the UK's most easterly town alongside college and specialist provision. Suffolk uses straight-line home-to-school distance as its oversubscription tie-breaker for community schools; the town's geography - bisected by Lake Lothing and the River Waveney - means that schools on either side of the water may be significantly further by road than the crow-flies distance suggests.

Secondary allocation in Lowestoft involves four schools with different specialisms and intake profiles, drawing from residential zones across Oulton Broad, Pakefield and Corton as well as the town centre. Families in outlying villages to the north and south of Lowestoft should note that Suffolk operates its own Rural Isolation priority criterion alongside standard distance, which can affect eligibility for specific community schools.

barnstaple.seoTitle: Barnstaple School Catchment Areas 2026 - 30 Schools, Postcode Checker
barnstaple.seoDescription: Barnstaple catchment finder: 24 primary + 2 secondary schools in Devon, every boundary mapped to your postcode. Ofsted ratings, 2026 admissions criteria and distances offered.
paragraphs: Barnstaple's 30 schools are administered by Devon County Council, with 24 primaries and 2 secondaries serving a North Devon market town that functions as the main education hub for a wide rural catchment stretching to Ilfracombe, Bideford and Exmoor fringes. Devon uses straight-line distance after sibling priority as the standard oversubscription criterion for community schools, though rural transport links and catchment-school designation add complexity for families in outlying villages.

Secondary provision in Barnstaple is dominated by Pilton Community College and Park Community School, which together serve a large geographic intake area that includes village schools from Bishops Tawton to Goodleigh. Devon's admissions allocation maps can differ substantially from school-published catchment boundaries, so families relying solely on a school's own information risk surprises at offer stage - using postcode-level mapping to check actual offer distances is strongly advised.

brentwood.seoTitle: Brentwood School Catchment Areas 2026 - 30 Schools, Postcode Checker
brentwood.seoDescription: Brentwood catchment finder: 19 primary + 5 secondary schools in Essex, every boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions, Ofsted ratings and distances offered.
paragraphs: Brentwood's 30 schools fall within Essex County Council's coordinated admissions scheme, covering 19 primaries and 5 secondaries in a commuter-belt town where strong rail links to London create high residential demand. Essex community schools use straight-line distance as the primary tie-breaker; secondary schools in Brentwood include both community and academy schools operating their own admissions arrangements, so criteria can differ significantly between institutions on the same street.

Primary catchment radii in Brentwood can be tight - Long Ridings and Warley have historically offered places to applicants within 400-600 metres in oversubscribed years. Families new to the area should check each school's specific admissions authority (Essex County Council for community schools, the school trust for academies) and consult offer-distance data from the preceding year, which catchment.school aggregates from each school's published admissions information.

southend-on-sea.seoTitle: Southend-on-Sea School Catchment Areas 2026 - 30 Schools, Postcode Checker
southend-on-sea.seoDescription: Southend-on-Sea catchment finder: 17 primary + 5 secondary schools, every boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distances offered.
paragraphs: Southend-on-Sea's 30 schools are administered by Southend-on-Sea City Council, covering 17 primaries and 5 secondaries alongside further education and specialist provision. Southend operates its own unitary authority admissions scheme, with community school criteria typically prioritising looked-after children, sibling links and measured straight-line distance in sequence. The town is notable for its two selective grammar schools - Southend High School for Boys and Southend High School for Girls - which draw applicants across Southend, Rochford and Castle Point based on the Southend grammar test.

Non-selective secondary allocation in Southend is affected by grammar school uptake, meaning community secondaries serve a mixed-ability cohort shaped by who has and has not taken the selective test. Families interested in selective grammar places should note that registration for the test usually opens well before primary Year 5 ends, with tests held in the autumn term of Year 6. For community schools, Southend's annual offer statistics show that the most popular primaries close within 0.5-0.8 kilometres in competitive years.

farnborough.seoTitle: Farnborough School Catchment Areas 2026 - 30 Schools, Postcode Checker
farnborough.seoDescription: Farnborough catchment finder: 20 primary + 3 secondary schools in Hampshire, every boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distances.
paragraphs: Farnborough's 30 schools fall under Hampshire County Council's coordinated admissions scheme, with 20 primaries and 3 secondaries serving a Rushmoor borough town known for its aerospace heritage and significant military population. Hampshire uses straight-line distance as the oversubscription tie-breaker for community schools after looked-after children and sibling priority; forces families benefit from Hampshire's additional admissions priority for children of Service personnel posted to an address within a school's normal area.

Secondary allocation in Farnborough involves schools across the Rushmoor boundary, with some families in southern Farnborough applying to schools in neighbouring Aldershot. The Cove and South Farnborough clusters of primaries serve distinct residential zones, and catchment distances can shift in years when a new housing development comes online - parents should use offer-distance data from the last two rounds to form realistic expectations before the September application deadline.

cannock.seoTitle: Cannock School Catchment Areas 2026 - 30 Schools, Postcode Checker
cannock.seoDescription: Cannock catchment finder: 20 primary + 5 secondary schools in Staffordshire, every boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distances.
paragraphs: Cannock's 30 schools are administered by Staffordshire County Council, covering 20 primaries and 5 secondaries across Cannock Chase district - a post-mining area bordered by Lichfield and Stafford. Staffordshire's community schools use straight-line distance as the final oversubscription criterion after looked-after children and sibling priority; secondary schools serving Cannock include Cannock Chase High School, Chase Terrace Academy and schools in Hednesford, which together account for the majority of Year 7 places in the district.

Primary catchment boundaries in Cannock can be compact because of the town's relatively high-density residential zones. Bridgtown, Five Ways and West Hill primaries serve distinct neighbourhoods, and the annual offer distances reflect demand that has grown as employment in the area has recovered. Families assessing school options in Cannock should check which secondary each feeder primary most commonly sends pupils to - this can inform primary choice significantly for families planning ahead.

leamington-spa.seoTitle: Leamington Spa School Catchment Areas 2026 - 30 Schools, Postcode Checker
leamington-spa.seoDescription: Leamington Spa catchment finder: 23 primary + 3 secondary schools in Warwickshire, every boundary mapped. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distances offered.
paragraphs: Leamington Spa's 30 schools are overseen by Warwickshire County Council, with 23 primaries and 3 secondaries serving Royal Leamington Spa and its surrounding parishes. Warwickshire uses straight-line distance as the oversubscription tie-breaker for community schools; the three secondaries serving the town - Campion School, Aylesford School and North Leamington School - each draw from specific residential zones and have historically offered places to applicants up to three kilometres away in competitive years.

Primary demand in Leamington is concentrated in the Old Town and Milverton wards, where period housing attracts families who often prioritise nearby primary schools with strong Ofsted profiles. New housing in the south of the town - around Whitnash and Sydenham - has added pressure to primaries such as Telford Infant and Whitnash, and catchment distances have tightened over recent years. Warwickshire publishes supplementary information forms for faith and academy schools that require separate application processes.

ceredigion.seoTitle: Ceredigion School Catchment Areas 2026 - 30 Schools, Postcode Checker
ceredigion.seoDescription: Ceredigion catchment finder: 30 schools across the county, every boundary mapped to your postcode. Welsh-medium and bilingual admissions, Ofsted equivalent ratings and distances.
paragraphs: Ceredigion's 30 schools are administered by Ceredigion County Council as part of a predominantly Welsh-medium education system where most schools teach through the medium of Welsh across all phases. Ceredigion applies a home-to-school distance criterion for oversubscription in community schools, but the county's linguistic policy means that catchment considerations are intertwined with Welsh-language medium of instruction preferences - families choosing English-medium provision may face longer travel times to appropriate schools.

The rural geography of Ceredigion means that several village schools serve tight local communities along the Teifi and Rheidol valleys, and school transport entitlement calculations are a significant practical consideration for many families. Parents who are new to the area should contact Ceredigion's School Admissions team early, as bilingual and Welsh-medium designation affects which schools are available as preference choices, and oversubscription in popular village schools can occur even where total pupil numbers appear modest.

hayes.seoTitle: Hayes School Catchment Areas 2026 - 29 Schools, Postcode Checker
hayes.seoDescription: Hayes catchment finder: 19 primary + 6 secondary schools in Hillingdon, every boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distances.
paragraphs: Hayes's 29 schools sit within the London Borough of Hillingdon's admissions remit, covering 19 primaries and 6 secondaries serving one of west London's most ethnically and culturally diverse communities. Hillingdon operates a distance-based tie-breaker for community schools alongside sibling and looked-after-children priority, with secondary school allocations coordinated centrally each spring through the pan-London secondary transfer system.

Demand for secondary places in Hayes is high, particularly for schools close to the Crossrail corridor that opened improved transport links to central London. Yeading and Minet primaries serve the north and south of the town respectively, and the annual offer statistics show that catchment distances for the most popular primaries can be as low as 0.4 kilometres in years of peak demand. Families planning secondary applications should also note that several faith schools in Hillingdon carry their own supplementary information requirements alongside the standard Hillingdon form.

hounslow.seoTitle: Hounslow School Catchment Areas 2026 - 29 Schools, Postcode Checker
hounslow.seoDescription: Hounslow catchment finder: 16 primary + 7 secondary schools, every boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distances offered.
paragraphs: Hounslow's 29 schools are administered by the London Borough of Hounslow, covering 16 primaries and 7 secondaries in an outer-west London borough closely linked to Heathrow and the affluent Chiswick and Kew fringes. Hounslow uses measured straight-line distance as the oversubscription tie-breaker for community schools; the borough coordinates secondary admissions through the pan-London system, with offers made on National Secondary Offer Day in March.

Competition for primary places in Hounslow town centre is acute - schools such as Hounslow Town and Wellington primaries have offered places to applicants within 0.3-0.5 kilometres in recent years. The borough also contains a number of faith schools with separate admissions criteria, including Catholic schools linked to the Brentford and Isleworth parishes. Families should verify whether their preferred school is a community school (Hounslow criteria) or an academy or faith school (school-specific criteria) before completing their application.

south-shields.seoTitle: South Shields School Catchment Areas 2026 - 29 Schools, Postcode Checker
south-shields.seoDescription: South Shields catchment finder: 21 primary + 3 secondary schools in South Tyneside, every boundary mapped. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distances offered.
paragraphs: South Shields's 29 schools are administered by South Tyneside Council, with 21 primaries and 3 secondaries serving a coastal town at the mouth of the River Tyne. South Tyneside uses straight-line distance as the oversubscription tie-breaker for community schools after looked-after children and sibling priority; the three secondary schools - Mortimer Community College, St Joseph's RC Academy and South Shields Grammar Technical School - serve distinct intake zones shaped by the town's terraced housing neighbourhoods.

Primary demand in South Shields centres on well-regarded schools such as Hadrian, Laygate and Stanhope, which serve the Westoe, Rekendyke and Cleadon Park communities. The town's position as a coastal settlement means that school numbers have been relatively stable, but regeneration around the river mouth and the expansion of Holborn and Westoe housing may affect catchment dynamics over the next admissions cycle. South Tyneside publishes its annual supplementary admissions information alongside the main prospectus in September.

penrith.seoTitle: Penrith School Catchment Areas 2026 - 29 Schools, Postcode Checker
penrith.seoDescription: Penrith catchment finder: 26 primary + 2 secondary schools in Westmorland and Furness, every boundary mapped. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distances.
paragraphs: Penrith's 29 schools fall within Westmorland and Furness Council's admissions scheme, covering 26 primaries and 2 secondaries in a historic market town that serves as the gateway to the Eden Valley and the northern Lake District. Westmorland and Furness was formed by the 2023 local government reorganisation of Cumbria, and its admissions policy for community schools retains a straight-line distance tie-breaker after sibling and looked-after-children priority.

Secondary provision in Penrith centres on Queen Elizabeth Grammar School - a partially selective school that draws applicants via an entrance assessment - alongside Ullswater Community College. Families not taking the grammar selection route compete for places at Ullswater, which serves a large rural catchment including villages such as Greystoke, Penruddock and Plumpton. The dispersed geography of the Eden Valley means that transport eligibility is a real consideration, as schools are often genuinely far from smaller settlements in the Pennines and Lakeland fringes.

worksop.seoTitle: Worksop Area School Catchment Finder 2026 - 29 Schools by Postcode
worksop.seoDescription: Worksop area schools: 24 primaries + 2 secondaries in Derbyshire, every catchment boundary mapped. Ofsted data, 2026 admissions criteria and distances offered.
paragraphs: The Worksop area spanning Derbyshire contains 29 schools - 24 primaries, 2 secondaries and 3 other settings - administered by Derbyshire County Council under its coordinated admissions scheme. Derbyshire uses straight-line distance as the tie-breaker for community schools after looked-after children and sibling priority; several of the primaries in this corridor, including Creswell and Whitwell schools, serve former pit villages where community identity is closely tied to the local school.

Secondary allocation in this Derbyshire border area is shaped by proximity to Worksop town itself and the transport links running south from Creswell toward Chesterfield. Families in the Worksop postcode boundary who are allocated Derbyshire schools should note that Nottinghamshire secondary provision may also be accessible depending on exact address, and checking both authorities' allocation data ensures the fullest picture of realistic secondary options.

folkestone.seoTitle: Folkestone School Catchment Areas 2026 - 29 Schools, Postcode Checker
folkestone.seoDescription: Folkestone catchment finder: 19 primary + 4 secondary schools in Kent, every boundary mapped to your postcode. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distances offered.
paragraphs: Folkestone's 29 schools are administered by Kent County Council, with 19 primaries and 4 secondaries in a Shepway coastal town that sits above the Channel Tunnel rail link and has undergone significant regeneration since the 2000s. Kent operates a selective grammar system for secondary education, meaning that the county's grammar schools draw high-attaining Year 6 applicants through the Kent Test, and non-grammar secondary schools - including Folkestone Academy and Pent Valley Technology College - serve the majority of the town's secondary-age cohort.

Primary catchment dynamics in Folkestone are influenced by the town's mix of Victorian terracing, newer harbour quarter development and rural fringe villages such as Hawkinge, Cheriton and Capel-le-Ferne. Sandgate and Capel primaries are popular with families in the coastal villages, and Kent's annual offer statistics show that distance tie-breakers for oversubscribed primaries can be as low as 0.6 kilometres in the town centre cluster. Families should factor in the Kent Test timeline for any secondary school planning, as registration typically opens in May of Year 5.

sutton.seoTitle: Sutton School Catchment Areas 2026 - 27 Schools by Postcode
sutton.seoDescription: Sutton catchment finder: 14 primary + 7 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. London Borough of Sutton 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Sutton has 27 schools - 14 primaries and 7 secondaries - within the London Borough of Sutton, one of the few London boroughs that retains selective grammar schools. Sutton Grammar School and Nonsuch High School for Girls are both single-sex selective schools drawing from across the borough and beyond, adding a significant grammar-versus-comprehensive dimension to secondary admissions in the area. Community primary schools use straight-line distance as the tiebreaker after siblings and looked-after children.

Demand for Cheam High School and Overton Grange School is consistently high among non-grammar applicants. Families in Sutton should be aware that applications for grammar school places require a separate entrance test in the autumn before the main admissions round. The borough borders Merton, Croydon, and Kingston upon Thames, so families near the boundary may wish to explore cross-borough options through the Pan-London co-ordinated admissions scheme.

bootle.seoTitle: Bootle School Catchment Areas 2026 - 18 Schools | Sefton
bootle.seoDescription: Bootle catchment finder: 13 primary + 3 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Sefton 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Bootle is a town on Merseyside within the Metropolitan Borough of Sefton, with 18 schools including 13 primaries and 3 secondaries. Sefton Council co-ordinates admissions for maintained schools, and most community primaries use catchment area or proximity as the main tiebreaker. Bootle's school population reflects a diverse, urban community with a significant Catholic presence - several schools are voluntary aided Catholic schools that apply faith-based criteria before distance.

The three secondary schools in Bootle are King's Leadership Academy Hawthornes, Hillside High School, and The Salesian Academy of St John Bosco, which is a Catholic school with national admissions criteria. Families in the outer parts of Bootle should check whether their address falls within Sefton or Liverpool's boundary, as the two councils operate separate admissions rounds, though each accepts out-of-borough preferences.

monmouthshire.seoTitle: Monmouthshire School Catchment Areas 2026 - Schools by Postcode
monmouthshire.seoDescription: Monmouthshire catchment finder: 28 schools mapped to your postcode in Monmouthshire, Wales. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted and Estyn ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Monmouthshire is a largely rural county in south-east Wales bordering the English counties of Gloucestershire and Herefordshire. The area has 28 state schools spread across market towns including Abergavenny, Caldicot, Chepstow, and Monmouth itself. Admissions are co-ordinated by Monmouthshire County Council in accordance with Welsh Government guidance, and most community schools use catchment zones aligned to local community boundaries.

Welsh-medium education is available through designated Welsh-medium schools and bilingual provision within Monmouthshire. Families considering secondary schools should note that Monmouthshire's secondary schools are grouped into feeder clusters; home addresses within each cluster are normally linked to a specific secondary school. Cross-border movement into English schools is possible but requires families to apply through the relevant English local authority.

beverley.seoTitle: Beverley School Catchment Areas 2026 - 20 Schools | East Yorkshire
beverley.seoDescription: Beverley catchment finder: 13 primary + 3 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. East Riding of Yorkshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Beverley is the county town of the East Riding of Yorkshire with 20 state schools - 13 primaries and 3 secondaries. East Riding of Yorkshire Council co-ordinates admissions and publishes annual catchment maps for community schools. The town's schools serve not just Beverley itself but also a wide rural hinterland of villages in the East Riding, making distance calculations important for families on the edge of the town.

Secondary admissions in Beverley are notable for including two selective schools: Beverley Grammar School (boys) and Beverley High School (girls), both of which select by ability for Year 7 entry. The selective tests are administered each autumn, and children who do not gain a selective place can apply for Longcroft School and Sixth Form College, which is the main comprehensive secondary for the area.

greenford.seoTitle: Greenford School Catchment Areas 2026 - 12 Schools | Ealing
greenford.seoDescription: Greenford catchment finder: 10 primary + 2 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Ealing 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.

The London Borough of Ealing co-ordinates all maintained school admissions through the Pan-London process. Ealing is known for oversubscribed primaries in areas close to well-regarded schools, where last-offered distances can be under a mile. Proximity (straight-line distance) is the main tiebreaker for community schools after siblings and looked-after children.

The two secondary schools serving Greenford are The Cardinal Wiseman Catholic School, a voluntary aided Catholic school with faith-based admissions criteria, and William Perkin Church of England High School, a Church of England academy. Families in Greenford who are not applying to faith schools should also consider cross-borough options in Harrow or Hillingdon, given Greenford's position near the borough boundary.

harpenden.seoTitle: Harpenden School Catchment Areas 2026 - 20 Schools | Hertfordshire

paragraphs: Harpenden is a prosperous Hertfordshire town with 20 state schools - 13 primaries and 4 secondaries. Hertfordshire County Council co-ordinates admissions using its 'home school' system: each address is linked to a designated catchment school, and families living in-catchment receive strong priority. Harpenden primaries are generally oversubscribed; catchment boundaries can be tight, and some streets fall into unexpected catchments due to historical boundary decisions.

Secondary schools in Harpenden include Roundwood Park School, Sir John Lawes School, St George's School (a Church of England voluntary aided school), and Katherine Warington School. Hertfordshire operates a linked feeder system for some schools, so which primary your child attends can influence secondary options. Families should check their home address on Hertfordshire's online school finder each year, as catchment boundaries are reviewed periodically.

witney.seoTitle: Witney School Catchment Areas 2026 - 29 Schools | Oxfordshire
witney.seoDescription: Witney catchment finder: 22 primary + 3 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Oxfordshire 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Witney is a fast-growing market town in west Oxfordshire with 29 schools - 22 primaries and 3 secondaries. Oxfordshire County Council co-ordinates admissions for community schools using a catchment area system, with in-catchment families receiving priority after looked-after children and siblings. Witney has seen significant housing development in the last decade, and some newer estates sit at the boundary between school catchments, making it essential to verify your address against the current maps.

The three secondary schools in Witney are Bartholomew School, The Henry Box School, and Wood Green School. All three are comprehensive academies. Witney is also served by some schools in nearby Carterton and the wider west Oxfordshire area, so families in the outer parts of town should explore all options. Oxfordshire's admissions timetable follows the national schedule with primary applications closing in January and secondary in October.

warwick.seoTitle: Warwick School Catchment Areas 2026 - 29 Schools | Warwickshire

Warwick is closely linked to Leamington Spa for schooling purposes, and families in the border areas between the two towns should check their designated school carefully, as some catchments extend across both town centres.

Secondary provision in Warwick is served by Myton School and Kineton High School, both comprehensive academies. Families should be aware that Warwickshire also has grammar schools in Stratford-upon-Avon, Alcester and Rugby, and some Warwick families explore grammar options through the Warwickshire grammar test. The county does not operate a full selective system but has a small number of grammar schools as legacy provision.

kingston-upon-thames.seoTitle: Kingston upon Thames School Catchment Areas 2026 - 28 Schools
kingston-upon-thames.seoDescription: Kingston upon Thames catchment finder: 13 primary + 3 secondary schools mapped to your postcode. Royal Borough 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance offered last year.
paragraphs: Kingston upon Thames is the administrative centre of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames, with 28 state schools - 13 primaries and 3 secondaries. The Royal Borough uses straight-line distance to the school gate as the tiebreaker for community schools after the usual priority groups. Kingston is among London's most sought-after boroughs, and popular primaries in the town centre and Surbiton can fill from very short distances.

Secondary admissions in Kingston are defined by the presence of two highly selective grammar schools: Tiffin School (boys) and The Tiffin Girls' School, both of which draw applicants from a much wider area and are among the most oversubscribed schools in England. The Kingston Academy is the main non-selective comprehensive in the borough. Families who do not secure a grammar place should apply early and list realistic non-selective options across both Kingston and neighbouring Richmond upon Thames.

Twickenham's primaries cover several distinct neighbourhoods including St Margarets, Whitton, and the riverside areas around Eel Pie Island.

Secondary schools in Twickenham include Waldegrave School (girls' comprehensive), Orleans Park School, Turing House School, and The Richmond upon Thames School. All are non-selective comprehensives; the borough has no grammar schools. The nearby Kingston upon Thames border means some Twickenham addresses may be closer to The Tiffin Girls' School or Tiffin School - although these are highly selective, some families in the south of Twickenham apply.

ellesmere-port.seoTitle: Ellesmere Port School Catchment Areas 2026 - 28 Schools | Cheshire

Secondary schools in Ellesmere Port are The Whitby High School, Ellesmere Port Church of England College, and Ellesmere Port Catholic High School. The Catholic school applies faith criteria before distance, so non-Catholic families should focus applications on the other two secondaries or look at schools in nearby Chester. torquay.seoTitle: Torquay School Catchment Areas 2026 - 28 Schools | Torbay

Torquay's secondary schools include Torquay Boys' Grammar School and Torquay Girls' Grammar School, both selective schools drawing from across Torbay and South Devon. Corby Technical School is a specialist technical school with a specific aptitude criterion. Northamptonshire has a small number of grammar schools in Wellingborough, Northampton and Kettering, but Corby itself has no selective provision. The area has seen significant population growth, so families should verify place availability with North Northamptonshire Council each cycle.

southall.seoTitle: Southall School Catchment Areas 2026 - 27 Schools | Ealing

Secondary schools in Southall include Villiers High School, Greenford High School, Featherstone High School, and Dormers Wells High School. Secondary provision in Batley is provided by Batley Girls' High School and Upper Batley High School, both of which serve distinct parts of the town. Kirklees does not have grammar schools, so all secondary places are allocated through the standard comprehensive admissions process. Families in Batley who wish to explore grammar options would need to consider schools in the Calderdale or Bradford areas, which operate separately from Kirklees.

Ten of the 18 schools are academies with independent admissions policies, and 4 have a faith character including the Catholic comprehensive St John Fisher Catholic College.

The three secondaries — St John Fisher Catholic College, Newcastle Academy, and Haywood Academy (also covering the Trent Vale area) — serve overlapping geographic zones. Staffordshire co-ordinates admissions through its annual School Admissions Guide. The town's proximity to Keele University and the wider Stoke-on-Trent conurbation means population density is higher to the east, where some primary catchments can be very tight. Families in rural parishes west of the town should check transport eligibility with Staffordshire Council before ranking schools.

redhill.seoTitle: Redhill School Catchment Areas 2026 - Surrey Schools & Admissions Guide
redhill.seoDescription: Redhill: 18 Surrey schools including St Bede's School. Catchment boundaries, Ofsted ratings and 2026 admissions criteria - free.
paragraphs: Redhill has 18 schools — 11 primaries and 3 secondaries — within Surrey County Council's co-ordinated admissions scheme. Eight of the 18 schools operate as academies with independent admissions policies, and 4 have a faith character. The area sits within Reigate and Banstead district and benefits from good transport links into London, driving strong demand for school places.

The main secondary schools in Redhill are St Bede's School, Carrington School, and Furzefield Primary and Secondary (which operates through Outwood Grange Academies Trust). Surrey County Council publishes its co-ordinated admissions scheme each September; secondary preference forms are due in October with national offer day in March. Families should note that Surrey's oversubscription criteria for community schools prioritise looked-after children, then siblings, then distance — and that Redhill's proximity to the M25 and commuter belt means last-offered distances at popular primaries have shortened considerably over the past decade.

thornton-heath.seoTitle: Thornton Heath School Catchment Areas 2026 - Croydon Schools Guide
thornton-heath.seoDescription: Thornton Heath: 17 Croydon schools with 2 outstanding Ofsted ratings. Catchment boundaries, admissions criteria and 2026 info - free.
paragraphs: Thornton Heath has 17 schools — 13 primaries and 1 secondary — within the London Borough of Croydon. Ten of the 17 schools operate as academies, and 2 have received an 'Outstanding' Ofsted judgment. Two schools have a faith character. Croydon co-ordinates all admissions through the London co-ordinated admissions process with national offer day in April.

The main secondary serving Thornton Heath is Norbury High School for Girls, a specialist girls' academy. Boys in the area are typically directed to mixed secondaries in neighbouring CR7 and SE25 postcodes — Croydon's school planning boundary means some Thornton Heath families fall within catchment of schools in neighbouring boroughs. Given London's cross-borough admissions flexibility, families are advised to consider schools in Lambeth and Merton alongside Croydon-maintained alternatives when submitting preferences.

ruislip.seoTitle: Ruislip School Catchment Areas 2026 - Hillingdon Schools & Admissions Guide
ruislip.seoDescription: Ruislip: 17 Hillingdon schools with 4 Ofsted Outstanding ratings. Catchment boundaries, admissions criteria and 2026 info - free.
paragraphs: Ruislip has 17 schools — 14 primaries and 3 secondaries — within the London Borough of Hillingdon. Notably, 4 of the 17 schools hold an 'Outstanding' Ofsted judgment, a high concentration for an area of this size. Four schools have a faith character, including Bishop Ramsey Church of England School at secondary level.

Secondary provision in Ruislip includes Queensmead School, Bishop Ramsey Church of England School, and Haydon School. Only 4 of the 17 schools are academies, meaning the majority follow Hillingdon's co-ordinated admissions criteria. Hillingdon operates the London co-ordinated scheme with a single preference form covering up to six schools; the borough's oversubscription criteria follow the standard looked-after children, sibling, then distance sequence. Popular Outstanding-rated primaries can offer places to applicants living within a few hundred metres in high-demand years.

surbiton.seoTitle: Surbiton School Catchment Areas 2026 - Kingston Schools & Admissions Guide
surbiton.seoDescription: Surbiton: 17 Kingston upon Thames schools with 2 Outstanding ratings. Catchment boundaries, admissions criteria and 2026 info - free.
paragraphs: Surbiton has 17 schools — 10 primaries and 3 secondaries — in the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames. Two schools have achieved 'Outstanding' Ofsted ratings, and 5 have a faith character. Six of the 17 operate as academies. Kingston coordinates admissions through the London co-ordinated scheme, with secondary preferences due in October.

The three secondary schools serving Surbiton are Tolworth Girls' School and Sixth Form, The Hollyfield School and Sixth Form Centre, and Chessington Community College. Tolworth Girls' is a specialist girls' school — boys seeking secondary places in Surbiton typically apply to Hollyfield or Chessington. The borough's Surrey border location means some Surbiton families also consider schools in Elmbridge and Epsom & Ewell; Kingston's admissions team can advise on out-of-borough processes. Primary demand in the KT5 and KT6 postcodes is high, with last-offered distances at sought-after schools often falling below half a mile.

willenhall.seoTitle: Willenhall School Catchment Areas 2026 - Walsall Schools & Admissions Guide
willenhall.seoDescription: Willenhall: 17 Walsall schools including St Thomas More Catholic School. Catchment boundaries, Ofsted ratings and 2026 admissions info - free.
paragraphs: Willenhall has 17 schools — 11 primaries and 3 secondaries — within Walsall Metropolitan Borough Council's co-ordinated admissions area. Seven of the 17 are academies and 3 have a faith character, including St Thomas More Catholic School at secondary level. Walsall co-ordinates maintained school admissions annually; secondary applications typically open in September with offers in March.

The three secondary schools serving Willenhall — St Thomas More Catholic School, Willenhall E-ACT Academy, and The Grange School — each set different oversubscription criteria. St Thomas More prioritises Catholic-faith applicants before distance; Willenhall E-ACT and The Grange use looked-after children, then siblings, then distance. The town borders both Wolverhampton and Walsall, and some families in the WV13 postcode find they sit within catchment of schools in both local authority areas — Walsall's admissions team can advise on cross-boundary applications.

holmfirth.seoTitle: Holmfirth School Catchment Areas 2026 - Kirklees Schools & Admissions Guide
holmfirth.seoDescription: Holmfirth: 17 Kirklees schools with 4 Outstanding Ofsted ratings. Catchment boundaries, admissions criteria and 2026 info - free.
paragraphs: Holmfirth has 17 schools — 15 primaries and 2 secondaries — in the Kirklees Metropolitan Council area. Four of the 17 hold 'Outstanding' Ofsted judgments, and 4 have a faith character. Six operate as academies. The area has a notably high proportion of outstanding primaries relative to its size, reflecting strong community engagement and stable pupil cohorts in the Colne Valley.

The two secondary schools are Holmfirth High School and Honley High School, both of which draw from a wide rural catchment across the upper Holme Valley. Kirklees operates a preference-based admissions scheme; families may express multiple preferences with Kirklees acting as the co-ordinating body. The valley geography means transport links strongly influence school choice — families in higher hamlets such as Holme and Hade Edge may qualify for home-to-school transport assistance. Secondary preference forms should be submitted by October for March offer day.

nantwich.seoTitle: Nantwich School Catchment Areas 2026 - Cheshire East Schools Guide
nantwich.seoDescription: Nantwich: 17 Cheshire East schools including Brine Leas School and Malbank College. Catchment boundaries, Ofsted ratings and 2026 admissions info - free.
paragraphs: Nantwich has 17 schools — 14 primaries and 2 secondaries — within Cheshire East Council's co-ordinated admissions scheme. Eleven of the 17 are academies, and 6 have a faith character, predominantly Church of England. Cheshire East co-ordinates maintained school admissions; secondary preferences are due in October with national offer day in March.

The two secondary schools, Brine Leas School and Malbank School and Sixth Form College, together serve virtually all of Nantwich's secondary-age pupils. Both are academies with their own oversubscription criteria — Brine Leas is mixed co-educational, while Malbank operates a sixth form providing post-16 provision for the wider area. Popular primaries in Nantwich town centre — particularly those close to the Weaver valley — can offer places to siblings and then prioritise distance, with last-offered distances at some schools falling below a mile in high-demand years.

launceston.seoTitle: Launceston School Catchment Areas 2026 - Cornwall Schools & Admissions Guide
launceston.seoDescription: Launceston: 17 Cornwall schools including Launceston College. Catchment boundaries, Ofsted ratings and 2026 admissions info - free.
paragraphs: Launceston has 17 schools — 16 primaries and 1 secondary — within Cornwall Council's co-ordinated admissions scheme. Twelve of the 17 operate as academies, reflecting Cornwall's unusually high academy conversion rate. Only 1 school has a faith character. Launceston sits on the Devon-Cornwall border, making it the main secondary catchment town for a large rural hinterland stretching from Bodmin Moor to the Tamar Valley.

Launceston College is the sole secondary school serving the town and surrounding villages, and as an academy it sets its own admissions policy — typically prioritising siblings and then distance. The vast rural catchment means the college draws pupils from as far as Callington, Camelford and North Tamerton. Cornwall Council's home-to-school transport policy provides assistance for pupils beyond 3 miles who live within the designated catchment area; families in outlying villages should check eligibility before applying. Primary applications in Cornwall close in January for September entry.

whitehaven.seoTitle: Whitehaven School Catchment Areas 2026 - Cumberland Schools Guide
whitehaven.seoDescription: Whitehaven: 17 Cumberland schools including The Whitehaven Academy. Catchment boundaries, Ofsted ratings and 2026 admissions info - free.
paragraphs: Whitehaven has 17 schools — 14 primaries and 2 secondaries — within Cumberland Council, formed in 2023 following the merger of Allerdale and Copeland councils. Seven of the 17 schools have a faith character, predominantly Roman Catholic, reflecting the town's historically strong Catholic community. Only 2 operate as academies, meaning the majority follow Cumberland's co-ordinated admissions framework.

The two secondary schools serving Whitehaven are The Whitehaven Academy and St Benedict's Catholic High School. St Benedict's prioritises Catholic-faith applicants before applying distance criteria; The Whitehaven Academy as an academy sets its own policy but broadly follows looked-after children, siblings, then proximity. Whitehaven's West Cumbrian coastal location and relative distance from larger urban centres mean it functions as a standalone admissions zone — families have few realistic alternatives outside the town, and the secondaries rarely close their catchments before the outer district boundary.

belper.seoTitle: Belper School Catchment Areas 2026 - Derbyshire Schools & Admissions Guide
belper.seoDescription: Belper: 17 Derbyshire schools including Belper School and The Ecclesbourne School. Catchment boundaries, Ofsted ratings and 2026 admissions info - free.
paragraphs: Belper has 17 schools — 14 primaries and 2 secondaries — within Derbyshire County Council's co-ordinated admissions area. Eight of the 17 are academies and 6 have a faith character, predominantly Church of England. One school holds an 'Outstanding' Ofsted judgment. Belper sits in the Derwent Valley, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and serves a mixture of town and semi-rural settlements.

The two secondary schools serving Belper are Belper School and Sixth Form Centre and The Ecclesbourne School in neighbouring Duffield. The Ecclesbourne is notably oversubscribed and attracts applicants from a wide geographic area including parts of Derby city; families should check last-offered distances carefully before relying on it as their first preference. Derbyshire County Council co-ordinates secondary admissions with national offer day in March; secondary preference forms are typically due in October. Primary demand in Belper town centre has tightened as residential development in the area has continued.

lytham-st-annes.seoTitle: Lytham St Annes School Catchment Areas 2026 – 9 Primary & 2 Secondary | Lancashire
lytham-st-annes.seoDescription: Lytham St Annes catchment finder: 14 Lancashire schools including St Bede's Catholic High and Lytham St Annes High School. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and catchment maps – free.
paragraphs: Lytham St Annes has 14 schools in the catchment.school database, including 9 primaries, 2 secondaries and 3 specialist settings, all administered by Lancashire County Council. Seven of the 14 schools hold a religious designation – Church of England, Roman Catholic or Christian – giving the town one of the higher faith-school ratios among Lancashire coast settlements. St Bede's Catholic High School and Lytham St Annes High School are the two secondary providers, each drawing from defined geographic catchment zones along the Fylde coast.

Lancashire uses road-measured distance rather than straight-line distance as the tiebreaker at oversubscribed community schools, so the precise route from your home to the school gate is what matters. At faith schools, supplementary information forms apply alongside catchment criteria. Two schools in the area are currently at or above their published admission numbers, so families whose address sits near a catchment boundary should check the most recent 'last distance offered' data before applying.

upminster.seoTitle: Upminster School Catchment Areas 2026 – 6 Primary & 4 Secondary | Havering
upminster.seoDescription: Upminster catchment finder: 12 Havering schools including The Coopers' Company and Coborn School. Avg fill rate 95%. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and distance data – free.
paragraphs: Upminster has 12 schools in the catchment.school database, including 6 primaries and 4 secondaries, all coordinated by Havering London Borough Council. With an average fill rate of 95% across schools with published capacity data – and 5 of 12 schools at or above their admission number – Upminster is one of the more competitive patches in Havering for school places. Six of the schools are academies that set their own admissions criteria independently of the council.

The four secondary schools – The Coopers' Company and Coborn School, Hall Mead School, Sacred Heart of Mary Girls' School and Gaynes School – each operate under different governance arrangements. The Coopers' Company and Coborn School, a selective grammar, uses aptitude tests alongside catchment distance, while Sacred Heart of Mary is a faith school with religious criteria. Families should review each school's individual admissions policy rather than relying on the council's standard oversubscription rules. All five schools with current Ofsted ratings are rated Good or Outstanding.

wellington.seoTitle: Wellington Somerset School Catchment Areas 2026 – 10 Primary & 1 Secondary | Somerset
wellington.seoDescription: Wellington Somerset catchment finder: 12 Somerset schools including Court Fields School. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and catchment boundary data – free.
paragraphs: Wellington in Somerset has 12 schools in the catchment.school database, with 10 primaries, 1 secondary and 1 special school, all coordinated by Somerset Council. Court Fields School is the town's single comprehensive secondary, drawing pupils from Wellington itself and the surrounding Somerset villages. Four of the 12 schools are academies, with the remaining schools following Somerset Council's standard admissions framework.

Five of the schools have a Church of England designation, reflecting the rural Somerset parish structure in which many village primaries are linked to their local church. The average fill rate across Wellington schools with published capacity data is 82%, and two schools are currently at or above their admission number. Somerset Council publishes annual catchment maps and last-distance-offered data each January for applications due in the following October.

deal.seoTitle: Deal Kent School Catchment Areas 2026 – 10 Primary & 1 Secondary | Kent
deal.seoDescription: Deal Kent catchment finder: 15 schools including Goodwin Academy. 11 academies, 7 faith schools. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and Kent catchment maps – free.
paragraphs: Deal in Kent has 15 schools in the catchment.school database, including 10 primaries, 1 secondary and 4 specialist settings. Goodwin Academy is the town's sole secondary school, serving Deal and surrounding coastal parishes under an academy trust arrangement. Eleven of the 15 schools in the area are academies, meaning each sets its own admissions criteria independently; it is important to read individual school policies rather than assuming Kent County Council's standard rules apply.

Seven schools hold a religious designation – Church of England or Roman Catholic – each running supplementary information forms alongside distance criteria. Kent County Council operates a partially selective county where around 25% of secondary places are grammar school places; Deal pupils sitting the 11-plus can access grammar schools in Dover and Sandwich. The average fill rate across Deal schools with published capacity data is 86%, with one school currently at or above its admission number.

malton.seoTitle: Malton School Catchment Areas 2026 – 11 Primary & 2 Secondary | North Yorkshire
malton.seoDescription: Malton North Yorkshire catchment finder: 13 schools including Norton College and Malton School. Avg fill 84%, 4 oversubscribed. 2026 admissions criteria and Ofsted ratings – free.
paragraphs: Malton in North Yorkshire has 13 schools in the catchment.school database, including 11 primaries and 2 secondaries – Norton College and Malton School. Both secondaries draw from a wide rural catchment taking in villages across the Ryedale district. North Yorkshire Council coordinates admissions, publishing annual oversubscription criteria and catchment boundary maps each September.

Seven of the 13 schools are academies operating under their own admissions policies, while four carry a Church of England or Roman Catholic designation. With an average fill rate of 84% and four schools currently at or above their published admission number, competition for places at popular primaries in the town centre is real. Six of the nine Ofsted-rated schools in the area are rated Good or Outstanding, and catchment distance tends to be tightest at those schools at the next intake.

newquay.seoTitle: Newquay School Catchment Areas 2026 – 10 Primary & 2 Secondary | Cornwall
newquay.seoDescription: Newquay catchment finder: 12 Cornwall schools including Newquay Tretherras and Treviglas Academy. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and catchment maps – free.
paragraphs: Newquay has 12 schools in the catchment.school database, including 10 primaries and 2 secondaries – Newquay Tretherras and Treviglas Academy – both of which are academies. Cornwall Council coordinates admissions for community schools, but with 10 of the 12 schools operating as academies, parents in Newquay need to apply to each school directly as well as through the council's coordinated round.

The average fill rate across Newquay schools with published capacity data is 79%, and two schools are currently at or above their admission number. Cornwall's rural catchment geography means that secondary transport routes and the distances between settlements matter more here than in urban areas: families outside the town boundary should confirm which secondary's catchment they fall into before applying. Five of the six Ofsted-rated schools in Newquay are rated Good or Outstanding.

leigh-on-sea.seoTitle: Leigh-on-Sea School Catchment Areas 2026 – 12 Primary & 2 Secondary | Southend-on-Sea
leigh-on-sea.seoDescription: Leigh-on-Sea catchment finder: 17 Southend schools with avg fill rate 99%. Eastwood Academy and Belfairs Academy. 5 oversubscribed primaries. 2026 admissions criteria – free.
paragraphs: Leigh-on-Sea has 17 schools in the catchment.school database, including 12 primaries and 2 secondaries – The Eastwood Academy and Belfairs Academy. It is one of the most competitive admissions areas in Essex: the average fill rate across schools with published capacity data is 99%, and five schools are currently at or above their published admission number. Families whose address is close to a catchment boundary face real uncertainty about securing their preferred school.

Eleven of the 17 schools are academies, each setting its own oversubscription criteria. One school has a Roman Catholic designation with faith-priority admissions. Southend-on-Sea City Council coordinates the admissions round but does not set criteria for academy schools. Six of the eight Ofsted-rated schools are rated Good or Outstanding – demand and catchment distance tend to be tightest at those schools. Checking the most recent 'last distance offered' data for each school is essential before the October application deadline.

alton.seoTitle: Alton Hampshire School Catchment Areas 2026 – 13 Primary & 2 Secondary | Hampshire
alton.seoDescription: Alton Hampshire catchment finder: 17 schools including Amery Hill School and Eggar's School. 8 faith schools. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and Hampshire catchment maps – free.
paragraphs: Alton in Hampshire has 17 schools in the catchment.school database, including 13 primaries and 2 secondaries – Amery Hill School and Eggar's School – coordinated by Hampshire County Council. Eight of the 17 schools carry a Church of England designation, the highest proportion of any market town of comparable size in the county, reflecting the dense network of village CofE primaries across the East Hampshire district.

Hampshire County Council uses straight-line distance as the oversubscription tiebreaker at community schools, alongside sibling priority. At the eight faith schools, supplementary information forms apply and faith criteria are assessed separately. The average fill rate across Alton schools with published capacity data is 85%, and one school is currently at or above its admission number. All five Ofsted-rated schools in the area are rated Good or Outstanding.

thirsk.seoTitle: Thirsk School Catchment Areas 2026 – 13 Primary & 1 Secondary | North Yorkshire
thirsk.seoDescription: Thirsk catchment finder: 17 North Yorkshire schools including Thirsk School & Sixth Form College. 9 of 10 Ofsted-rated schools rated Good or Outstanding. 2026 admissions – free.
paragraphs: Thirsk in North Yorkshire has 17 schools in the catchment.school database, including 13 primaries, 1 secondary (Thirsk School & Sixth Form College) and 3 other settings, coordinated by North Yorkshire Council. Thirsk is notable for the quality of its school provision: nine of the ten Ofsted-rated schools in the area are rated Good or Outstanding – the highest such proportion among North Yorkshire's market towns. Eight schools carry a Church of England or Roman Catholic designation.

With eight academies among the 17 schools, parents need to check individual admissions policies in addition to North Yorkshire Council's coordinated scheme. Three schools are currently at or above their published admission number, and the average fill rate is 81%. The wide rural catchment of Thirsk School & Sixth Form College takes in villages across the Hambleton district; home-to-school transport eligibility and catchment boundary maps are available from North Yorkshire Council's admissions team.

towcester.seoTitle: Towcester School Catchment Areas 2026 – 14 Primary & 2 Secondary | West Northamptonshire
towcester.seoDescription: Towcester catchment finder: 17 West Northamptonshire schools including Sponne School and Silverstone UTC. 11 faith schools. 2026 admissions criteria and Ofsted ratings – free.
paragraphs: Towcester in West Northamptonshire has 17 schools in the catchment.school database, including 14 primaries and 2 secondaries – Sponne School and the specialist Silverstone UTC – coordinated by West Northamptonshire Council. Eleven of the 17 schools carry a Church of England designation, making Towcester one of the most faith-heavy admissions areas in Northamptonshire. This matters practically: faith criteria run alongside distance at all 11 CofE schools, meaning catchment distance alone does not determine a place.

Eight of the 17 schools are academies, each publishing their own oversubscription criteria separately from the council's coordinated round. The average fill rate is 74% and two schools are currently at or above their admission number. Seven of eight Ofsted-rated schools are rated Good or Outstanding. Silverstone UTC is a University Technical College specialising in engineering and motorsport technology, with its own application process and national catchment – families interested in that provision should apply directly to the school.

dorking.seoDescription: Dorking catchment finder: 17 Surrey schools including The Ashcombe School and The Priory CofE School. 11 faith schools. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and Surrey catchment maps – free.
paragraphs: Dorking in Surrey has 17 schools in the catchment.school database, including 9 primaries, 2 secondaries – The Ashcombe School and The Priory Church of England School – and 6 other settings. Eleven of the 17 schools hold a religious designation (Church of England or Roman Catholic), the highest faith-school concentration in Surrey's commuter belt outside central Guildford. Each faith school publishes its own supplementary information form and faith-criteria assessment schedule.

Surrey County Council uses straight-line distance as the oversubscription tiebreaker at community schools. Ten schools are academies setting their own admissions rules. The average fill rate is 77%, and one school is currently at or above its admission number. All three Ofsted-rated schools in the area are rated Good or Outstanding. Surrey's annual School Admissions prospectus, published each September, includes the most recent 'last distance offered' data for each oversubscribed school in the Mole Valley area.

erith.seoTitle: Erith School Catchment Areas 2026 – 13 Primary & 1 Secondary | Bexley
erith.seoDescription: Erith catchment finder: 16 Bexley schools including Leigh Academy Bexley. 12 academies, avg fill 80%. 2026 admissions criteria, Ofsted ratings and London catchment maps – free.
paragraphs: Erith in the London Borough of Bexley has 16 schools in the catchment.school database, including 13 primaries and 1 secondary – Leigh Academy Bexley – plus 2 other settings. Twelve of the 16 schools are academies operating under their own admissions frameworks, making Erith one of the most academy-heavy areas in South East London. Four schools hold a religious designation (Church of England or Roman Catholic), each with faith-priority criteria assessed via supplementary information form.

Bexley Council coordinates the borough-wide admissions round but does not set criteria for academy schools, so families need to review each school's policy individually. The average fill rate across Erith schools with published capacity data is 80%, and two schools are currently at or above their admission number. Six of the seven Ofsted-rated schools are rated Good or Outstanding. London's common application window opens in September for primary places (January deadline) and September for secondary places (October deadline).

wallington.seoTitle: Wallington School Catchment Areas 2026 – 9 Primary & 3 Secondary | Sutton
wallington.seoDescription: Wallington catchment finder: 16 Sutton schools including Wilson's School, Wallington High School for Girls and Wallington County Grammar. All 6 Ofsted-rated schools are Good or Outstanding. 2026 admissions – free.
paragraphs: Wallington in the London Borough of Sutton has 16 schools in the catchment.school database, including 9 primaries and 3 secondaries – Wilson's School, Wallington High School for Girls, and Wallington County Grammar School. All three secondaries are selective grammar schools, which is highly unusual in London: Sutton is one of only two London boroughs that retains full academic selection at secondary level. Entry is via the consortium grammar school test held each September.

All six Ofsted-rated schools in Wallington are rated Good or Outstanding, and with four schools currently at or above their admission number and an average fill rate of 85%, competition for places at the most sought-after schools is sustained. Four schools hold a religious designation (Church of England or Roman Catholic). Families seeking non-selective secondary provision will typically need to look beyond Wallington to neighbouring Sutton or Croydon areas, or apply to a faith school under its own admissions criteria.

cramlington.seoTitle: Cramlington School Catchment Areas 2026 – 12 Primary & 1 Secondary | North Tyneside
cramlington.seoDescription: Cramlington catchment finder: 16 North Tyneside schools including Cramlington Learning Village. Avg fill 90%, 3 oversubscribed. 2026 admissions criteria and Ofsted ratings – free.
paragraphs: Cramlington in North Tyneside has 16 schools in the catchment.school database, including 12 primaries, 1 secondary – Cramlington Learning Village – and 3 other settings, coordinated by Northumberland County Council. Cramlington Learning Village is a large all-through academy drawing secondary pupils from across the Cramlington new town area. The school's size and reputation mean secondary places attract applications from beyond the immediate catchment.

The average fill rate across Cramlington schools with published capacity data is 90%, and three schools are currently at or above their published admission number. Two schools hold a religious designation (Church of England or Roman Catholic). Northumberland County Council publishes annual admissions guidance each September; families near the boundary between Cramlington's catchment and neighbouring areas in North Tyneside should confirm which authority's round to apply through. Three of four Ofsted-rated schools in the area are rated Good or Outstanding.

bideford.seoTitle: Bideford School Catchment Areas 2026 – 13 Primary & 2 Secondary | Devon
bideford.seoDescription: Bideford catchment finder: 16 Devon schools including Bideford College and Atlantic Academy. Avg fill 89%, 3 oversubscribed. 2026 admissions criteria and Ofsted ratings – free.
paragraphs: Bideford in Devon has 16 schools in the catchment.school database, including 13 primaries and 2 secondaries – Bideford College and Atlantic Academy – coordinated by Devon County Council. The rural hinterland around Bideford – including villages in Torridge district – feeds into the town's primary and secondary schools, so transport routes and the 'last distance offered' data for each school are important planning inputs. Five of the seven Ofsted-rated schools in the area are rated Good or Outstanding.

bedlington.seoDescription: Bedlington catchment finder: 8 Northumberland schools including Bedlington Academy and St Benet Biscop Catholic Academy. 2026 admissions criteria and Ofsted ratings – free.
paragraphs: Bedlington in Northumberland has 8 schools in the catchment.school database, including 6 primaries and 2 secondaries – Bedlington Academy and St Benet Biscop Catholic Academy – coordinated by Northumberland County Council. Northumberland County Council publishes annual admissions maps each autumn; families in the surrounding East Bedlington area should confirm catchment boundaries before the January primary application deadline.

malmesbury.seoTitle: Malmesbury School Catchment Areas 2026 – 7 Primary & 1 Secondary | Wiltshire
malmesbury.seoDescription: Malmesbury catchment finder: 8 Wiltshire schools including Malmesbury School. 7 faith schools, avg fill 79%. 2026 admissions criteria and Ofsted ratings – free.
paragraphs: Malmesbury in Wiltshire has 8 schools in the catchment.school database, including 7 primaries and 1 secondary – Malmesbury School – coordinated by Wiltshire Council. The average fill rate across Malmesbury schools with published capacity data is 79%, and two schools are currently at or above their admission number. Wiltshire Council uses straight-line distance as the standard oversubscription tiebreaker at community schools. All six Ofsted-rated schools in the area are rated Good or Outstanding. Families in the rural parishes west of Malmesbury should check catchment boundaries carefully, as some villages feed into Tetbury or Cirencester schools rather than Malmesbury School.

ripon.seoTitle: Ripon School Catchment Areas 2026 – 13 Primary & 2 Secondary | North Yorkshire
ripon.seoDescription: Ripon catchment finder: 16 North Yorkshire schools including Ripon Grammar School and Outwood Academy Ripon. 11 faith schools. 2026 admissions criteria and Ofsted ratings – free.
paragraphs: Ripon in North Yorkshire has 16 schools in the catchment.school database, including 13 primaries and 2 secondaries – Ripon Grammar School and Outwood Academy Ripon – coordinated by North Yorkshire Council. Faith criteria run alongside distance at all 11 designated schools.

Families seeking a non-selective secondary option apply to Outwood Academy Ripon, which operates under an academy trust's own admissions criteria. Eight schools are academies.
